:PROPERTIES:
:CATEGORY: Queue
:ID:       eaeeb4ee-ceee-4094-8598-bbcdc8214b66

- State "DOING"      from "TODO"       [2026-08-22 Sat 22:56] \\
  investigate why clock pairs are dropped
- [2026-08-22 Sat 22:56]--[2026-08-22 Sat 23:14] find why explicit clock pairs are dropped
- State "DONE"       from "DOING"      [2026-08-22 Sat 23:14] \\
  brackets authoritative, verified live
:END:
:PLAN:

*Measured 2026-08-22, on the previous day's own queue.* The 2026-08-21 files hold *twelve* =clock_in=/=clock_out= pairs, each carrying a heading =:ID:= and a human-written note -- "guard auto-promote against containers and batches" on =42808717= from 13:07:36 to 13:16:20, then =e30d52d7=, =cd1e974e=, =dd2399c0= in sequence. Every one is =applied: false=. The review pass offered instead a *single* unassigned span, =10:37--13:24=, and asked which one heading it belonged to. The human picked [[id:a279216c-38db-478c-ba52-ad31c87fbfd9][a279216c]] -- a cosmetic item explicitly off the critical path that nobody had opened -- and an hour of implementation work on five headings landed there.

*The capability is not missing; it fired for one heading and not the others.* =config.el= already builds =clock= items by pairing =clock_in= with =clock_out=, and already resolves "the enclosing =clock_in='s note" when labelling a span. The 2026-08-21 day node proves the path works end to end: its pair became a suggested item and applied as 0:09 in 4 runs. The four headings clocked in the same session, by the same session, produced no CLOCK line at all. *That asymmetry is the bug, and finding it is this heading's work* -- it is an investigation, not a design.

*The reframing it forces, which is worth more than the fix.* Attribution has been treated as a *reconstruction* problem -- guess the heading from timestamps at review -- and every increment has gone into guessing better: the suggester, its container guard, [[id:5a6d2c75-9a42-4dd4-b4d6-670aeebc5b46][5a6d2c75]]'s evidence rendering, [[id:1a5a5254-f62d-46e7-9a6c-3d84f2f52873][1a5a5254]]'s power assertions. But it is a *recording* problem: the session knew what it was working on, said so, and the record was discarded. [[id:62c6b1be-4e3c-4ea1-9f0c-19ee70be0e1e][62c6b1be]] diagnosed the same day's failure as insufficient discipline -- "calling =org_clock_in= exactly once" -- and the fix was read as "call it more often". On 2026-08-21 it was called twelve times, correctly, and the outcome was identical. The discipline half is done; the consumption half is missing.

*What it enables once consumed, in order of value:* a work-run falling inside a =clock_in=/=clock_out= interval is attributed with *certainty* and needs no human at all; a span is then *partitioned* by the pairs it contains rather than assigned whole; and only the residue -- runs no pair covers -- reaches a person. On the measured day that would have auto-assigned roughly 24 minutes across twelve headings correctly and left a much smaller, more local question. 5a6d2c75's evidence then matters for the residue, which is the case it was actually written for.

*Diagnosed 2026-08-22, and it is two mechanisms rather than the one the heading assumed.*

The =:agent-id= gate on the pairing loop in =--review-items-from-queue= is not the bug. It is deliberate: a main-lane bracket can span human idle, so duration is meant to come from guideposts *subdividing* the bracket, while the pair contributes attribution (via =--queue-events-by-id='s lane tracking) and the span's label. =:suggested= names exactly that split.

*The operative defect is downstream.* Guideposts are turn boundaries -- =Stop= and =UserPromptSubmit= -- so a bracket opened and closed inside a *single turn* contains none of them, yields no span, and produces no item at all. Continuous, uninterrupted work is precisely the case that vanishes.

The interleaved queue for session =44ebddaf= on 2026-08-21 is the proof, and needs no interpretation:

: 13:07:10 resume
: 13:07:36 clock_in  42808717
: 13:11:01 block_start
: 13:12:52 block_end
: 13:16:20 clock_out
: 13:16:56 clock_in  e30d52d7
: 13:20:25 clock_out
: 13:20:46 clock_in  cd1e974e
: 13:21:46 clock_out
: 13:22:08 clock_in  dd2399c0
: 13:22:38 clock_out
: 13:24:41 pause

Fifteen minutes, four brackets, *zero* pause/resume between the first =clock_in= and the last =clock_out=. By contrast the 2026-08-21 day node's bracket -- 14:53:42 to 15:42:08 -- straddles many turns, so its inside guideposts clustered and it applied as 0:09 in 4 runs. *That is the whole asymmetry*: an item appears iff a turn boundary happens to fall inside the bracket. It also explains why the =DONE= transitions all applied while the CLOCK lines did not -- =todo= events emit an item unconditionally, with no guidepost dependency.

*Two traps the naive fix walks into, both visible in the same data.*

1. Emitting each main-lane pair as one whole item re-imports the overcount =--span-work-runs= exists to kill: the day node's bracket is 48m26s of wall clock against ~9m of actual runs. Pairs must be authoritative for *attribution*, not for duration -- which is what this heading already said, and the implementation has to honour: a pair bounds the interval, runs subdivide it.
2. The pair endpoints must also be excised from the *orphan* stream, or the fix mints the double-count it is chasing. =resume 13:07:10= and =pause 13:24:41= are both orphans (the lane is empty at both moments) and are *adjacent* in the orphan stream, since everything between them is bracket-attributed -- and a =resume= -> =pause= adjacency never splits however long the gap. The unassigned span would straddle all four brackets by construction. Pair intervals want the treatment block intervals already get in =--aggregate-guideposts=.

*Bracket edges are recoverable and are currently thrown away.* =clock_in 14:53:42= -> =pause 14:54:44= and =resume 15:41:17= -> =clock_out 15:42:08= appear in no span today, because the guidepost filter drops the =clock_in=/=clock_out= events before the runs are computed. Treating the endpoints as =resume=/=pause= respectively recovers both, and is a discriminating test.

:END:
*Shipped 2026-08-22* on =feature/authoritative-clock-pairs=.

A main-lane bracket now emits its own review item, =:origin 'bracketed=, carrying the pair's *own* note rather than the first =clock_in= note anywhere in the heading's events -- =cc0c17a7= was clocked on two days with two different notes and both spans wore the earlier one. The =:agent-id= distinction is *kept*, because the reasoning behind it was sound: a subagent's interval stays =:suggested= nil and is written end to end, while a main-lane bracket is =:suggested= t and subdivided into runs. The bracket's own endpoints are now read as run boundaries, so a bracket with no guideposts inside yields one run covering it and a bracket full of them is subdivided as before.

*Three further defects surfaced on the way, each measured, none of them anticipated:*

1. *=--block-intervals= returned nil on every production call.* Callers filtered events to pause/resume before handing them over, so the block markers were gone before anything looked for them. The permission-block feature ([[id:f4e628ce-e653-429a-8f3c-0f5d4241b139][f4e628ce]]) was inert for as long as it had existed, and its tests passed throughout because they hand the block events straight to =--aggregate-guideposts= and so never cross the filter that was dropping them.
2. *The idle floor merged the two sides of a permission wait back together.* The measured block is 1m51s against a 120s floor, so splitting the runs was necessary but not sufficient -- =--apply-idle-floor= now takes barriers it will not merge across.
3. *Subdividing from the pending queue alone sees an empty bracket.* A bracket's inside guideposts are usually applied long before the bracket is, because a pause/resume pair reaches review as a span on the day it happens while the bracket sits unconsumed. With the pending group alone the day node offered 48 minutes as one unbroken run. Subdivision now reads the full history; emission stays pending-only. Same lesson as =--review-suggest-heading='s, and it was written down there already.

*Verified live, not only in batch.* 345 tests, 344 as expected -- the one failure (=clock-report-block-today=) fails identically on the unmodified tree and is unrelated. Five of the seven new tests fail with =config.el= reverted and the tests kept, so they discriminate; the other two are deliberate regression guards asserting *unchanged* behaviour (a subagent interval stays authoritative, an unmatched =clock_in= still reaches review through the residue path) and pass both ways by design.

End to end over the real 2026-08-21 queue, read-only: all twelve pairs produce items with their own notes, and the four-session total falls from 297.5 to 155.0 minutes written. =42808717= is 0:08 in 2 runs with the 1m51s wait excised; the day node is 0:11 in 6 rather than 48 minutes whole. Then re-verified through the running Emacs via =org_pending_updates=, which is what proves the reload took: 78 items across 51 headings, against *one* before.

*Two things a reader should expect rather than treat as defects.* Two of the twelve write no CLOCK line at all -- they are 30s and 5s and render as =0:00=, which the existing rendered-zero rule refuses; that rule is unchanged and honest. And the review buffer now surfaces a large backlog of bracketed items reaching back to 2026-08-11, because every one of them was being silently discarded. That is the bug's own history becoming visible, not new work appearing.

*The record it now contradicts.* The hour of 2026-08-21 implementation work is already applied to [[id:a279216c-38db-478c-ba52-ad31c87fbfd9][a279216c]], and the day node already carries its 0:09. The correct items are pending over an already-wrong record, so reconciling the two is a human decision in the review buffer, not something apply should be taught to do. [[id:2d100d0d-2d04-43b9-af1e-f4d6b52bbada][2d100d0d]]'s cross-item overlap check remains a separate heading and is now much cheaper: a span partitioned by the brackets it contains cannot overlap them.

Captured 2026-08-07 from conversation. Proposal: TODO.org (live) →
DONE.org (archive) → a terse, permanent, conventional-timeline changelog,
so DONE.org can be pruned or semantically compressed as work recedes
without losing the record entirely.

*Measured first, because the diagnosis moves:* DONE.org holds 22 entries
and 955 lines, every one archived on =2026-07-29= or =-07-30= — archiving
has not run since. Meanwhile TODO.org is 2444 lines and still carries
*13* =DONE=/=CANCELLED= headings, the oldest at line 7. The pressure is
not tier 2 overflowing; it is tier 1→2 having stalled, so completed work
accumulates in the live file. A third tier added now would relieve none
of that. Restore the archiving cadence first and re-measure — tier 3 may
not be needed for a long time.

*If built anyway, three constraints:*
- *Referential integrity is the real risk.* 21 distinct =[[id:...]]=
  links point into archived headings today, from other org files,
  CLAUDE.md, and the auto-memory folder — two of them added
  2026-08-07 citing =6a6d5b4e=. A conventional Markdown changelog has no
  stable per-entry identifier, so pruning breaks every inbound link
  silently. Any tier-3 format must carry the original =:ID:=, or leave an
  ID-bearing stub behind in DONE.org.
- *Git is already a chronological changelog*, so the question is what
  this adds. The honest answer: git records what *changed*; DONE.org
  records what was *learned* and why the obvious approach failed. That is
  the part with no other home — and it means tier 3's content should be
  biased toward decisions and dead ends, not shipped features, which git
  already covers.
- *Compression is where this project's signature failure mode lives.*
  The most valuable sentence in =6a6d5b4e= is that the initial hypothesis
  was a red herring — precisely what terse summarization drops first,
  because it does not look like an outcome. Editorial rule: keep what
  would change a future decision, drop what is re-derivable from the
  code. Model-driven compression without human review is the same
  confidently-wrong pattern [[id:b5f7c5c7-7ad6-4c68-9cce-3479db1f1644][b5f7c5c7]]
  exists to eliminate; make it diffable and reviewed.

*Format: stay in org, don't leave for Markdown.* =org-archive.el= already
supports =datetree/= in =org-archive-location= (org-archive.el:284), so
=#+ARCHIVE: DONE.org::datetree/* Done= buys chronological structure with
no new code, while preserving =[[id:]]= resolution, =org-ql=
queryability, and tags. A =CHANGELOG.md= discards all of that for the
keepachangelog convention, which is release-oriented — and this project
has no releases. Checked per
[[id:c084553c-0621-4a96-9fa1-f32850aeec6a][c084553c]]'s standing
instruction to exhaust org's own machinery first.

Open: what triggers a prune (size, age, or deliberate act — probably
deliberate); whether tier 3 is its own =CHANGELOG.org= or a datetree
inside DONE.org; and whether anything should enumerate inbound =[[id:]]=
references before a prune, since nothing does today.

:END:
*Cancelled 2026-08-21, and the re-measure this heading asked for is the reason.* Its own instruction was "restore the archiving cadence first and re-measure -- tier 3 may not be needed for a long time." Re-measured: DONE.org has gone 955 -> 9554 lines and 22 -> 63 entries, but TODO.org still carries *30* finished headings against the 13 recorded above, and the newest =:ARCHIVE_TIME:= in the file is =2026-08-17=. The original diagnosis therefore holds and has worsened: the pressure is tier 1->2 stalling, not tier 2 overflowing, and a third tier would still relieve none of it.

*Superseded rather than merely deferred*, which is why this is CANCELLED and not left at MAYBE. Both jobs a third tier was for now have owners. Semantic compression is answered at the *body* level by the 2026-08-20 retention policy recorded at [[id:3063c3e5-0dd0-4354-8985-271b0313c5d1][3063c3e5]] -- a closed body holds a concise debrief, the problem statement and plan move to a drawer. And "git is already a chronological changelog, so what does this add" is answered by [[id:41cf5830-fc2e-4dc6-b243-a0c2718a53a3][41cf5830]], an index into git rather than a retelling of it. A third *file* has no remaining unique job.

*One fact kept deliberately, because it outlives the proposal.* The referential-integrity constraint is now much larger than when it was written: 21 inbound =[[id:]]= links into archived headings then, 353 id links across the live documents today. Any future pruning or compression of DONE.org must carry the original =:ID:= or leave an ID-bearing stub, or it breaks inbound links silently. That constraint belongs to whoever eventually compresses DONE.org, not to this heading.

*And it leaves one thing unowned, which is the real finding of the re-measure.* Archiving *cadence*. [[id:38b92521-bba4-4bb5-9cd9-465862471a72][38b92521]] ran the archive once and closed on 2026-08-17 -- the same date as the newest =:ARCHIVE_TIME:=. Nothing owns the recurring pass, and 30 finished headings sitting in the live file is a direct contribution to [[id:b07df584-3adc-433c-ab49-e104f88aecf7][b07df584]]'s context-cost complaint.

*Observed live 2026-08-21, on this repo's own file.* Five children were captured under [[id:a1d63f52-4c07-4b9e-8f31-6d2b90c4e7a5][a1d63f52]] in one session, each keywordless, each with a =todo -> TODO= event queued. The human applied the queue, and one of them came out =NEXT=:

#+BEGIN_EXAMPLE
- State "TODO"       from              [2026-08-21 Fri 09:52]
- State "NEXT"       from "TODO"       [2026-08-21 Fri 10:27] \\
  Auto-promoted: sole remaining TODO in its sibling group.
#+END_EXAMPLE

Nobody chose it. =claude-code-ide-org--trigger-auto-promote-sole-todo= promotes the lone =TODO= in a sibling group when no sibling is =NEXT=, and *during a batch apply that condition is true transiently*: the review pass applies one event at a time, so the moment the first child's keyword lands it is the only keyworded sibling of five. Group size counts all siblings, so the size >= 2 guard passes. The promotion is correct by the trigger's own rule and meaningless in fact -- it records apply order, not judgement.

*It also lands on the wrong heading in a way that matters.* Here the child that must genuinely go first was [[id:e30d52d7-960b-44f3-ab92-93846c81a1bd][e30d52d7]], which has a hard ordering constraint the others do not; =NEXT= went to whichever event the queue happened to hold first. A reader who trusts =NEXT= gets the opposite of the ordering the bodies argue for.

*Self-correcting, but only if someone notices.* Setting the right sibling =NEXT= makes =--trigger-demote-conflicting-next= put the stray one back to =TODO= with a note, so no cleanup is needed beyond the correction itself. The cost is that the wrong =NEXT= is indistinguishable from a real one until read closely -- the =:LOGBOOK:= note is the only tell.

*The third instance of one shape*, which is the reason to record it rather than fix it quietly. =--trigger-auto-promote-sole-todo= counts siblings and checks nothing else: [[id:42808717-2736-4bf4-872e-887f990203ca][42808717]] is the same trigger promoting a *container*, and [[id:62c6b1be-4e3c-4ea1-9f0c-19ee70be0e1e][62c6b1be]] was =--review-suggest-heading= naming a container for the same underlying reason -- a predicate reading state without asking whether the heading is the kind of thing the answer should apply to. Worth fixing together with 42808717, since both are guards on the same function.

*Possible shapes, none chosen:* suppress the trigger while a review pass is applying (the apply already runs as one command, so it has a natural window); require the group to have been stable rather than mid-batch; or -- simplest -- decline to promote when the group contains keywordless siblings, since that is precisely the signature of a half-applied batch.

:END:
*Shipped 2026-08-21* with [[id:42808717-2736-4bf4-872e-887f990203ca][42808717]]. None of the three shapes recorded above was taken as written.

*"Decline when the group holds keywordless siblings" was rejected*, despite being the simplest. A capture whose =todo -> TODO= event the human dismisses at review stays keywordless for good, and its group then silently never auto-promotes again -- a missing NEXT nobody can see, where the defect it replaces is a wrong NEXT anyone can demote. It also collides with the permanent keywordless scaffolding [[id:e30d52d7-960b-44f3-ab92-93846c81a1bd][e30d52d7]] is about to introduce.

*What shipped is suppress-then-settle.* =--review-apply= binds a new batch-scoped =--review-applying= around its loop; the trigger declines while it is bound; =--review-settle-auto-promote= then runs the trigger once per touched heading, against the batch's finished state. Only =state= items settle -- nothing else moves a keyword, and a capture writes its heading without one.

*Suppression alone was considered and rejected.* Under the queue architecture nearly every real transition arrives through apply, so a trigger that only declined there would be live in its tests and dead in production -- the shape =--trigger-auto-clock-in='s own docstring already flags as worth avoiding. The settle pass keeps the rule and changes only *when* it is evaluated.

*A new flag rather than reusing =--auto-clock-in-active=*, which =--review-apply-item= binds per *item* as one function's clock re-entrancy guard. What must not be seen here is the half-applied state *between* items, which is a property of the batch.

*Verified by mutation.* Dropping the suppression fails only the new apply-order test; dropping the settle pass fails only the sole-survivor test, whose whole job is to catch a suppress-only fix. Confirmed live in the running Emacs after =load-file=: three children applied as one batch all end TODO with zero =Auto-promoted= lines.

=claude-code-ide-org--trigger-auto-promote-sole-todo= promotes the sole
remaining =TODO= in a sibling group to =NEXT=. It counts siblings and
checks nothing else — so when that sole survivor is a *container*, the
promotion declares a project to be an action.

Reproduced 2026-08-19 on a scratch file, after setting the only =NEXT=
sibling to =DONE=:

: ** DONE Ordinary sibling
: ** NEXT An epic with children
: *** TODO A real child action
:   Auto-promoted: sole remaining TODO in its sibling group.

The epic is now =NEXT= while its own child action is merely =TODO=,
which inverts the one thing =NEXT= is supposed to mean.

*The guard already exists and is simply not used here.*
=claude-code-ide-org--container-heading-p= is what exempts containers
from =--trigger-auto-clock-in=, on an argument that applies verbatim:
CLAUDE.md holds that an epic is emergent — "a heading that has acquired
children carrying TODO keywords" — and
[[id:ab75d6d2-0e59-405d-92c6-2c67488db133][ab75d6d2]] measured the cost
of treating one as a leaf. Two triggers sit on the same hook; one
consults the predicate and the other does not.

*Found by checking something that turned out to be correct.* The user
asked whether setting =NEXT= on a subtask affects only its siblings and
never toggles the parent. It does exactly that, verified both
directions: a child going =NEXT= left its parent and an unrelated
top-level =NEXT= untouched, and a top-level heading going =NEXT= demoted
its top-level sibling while leaving a child's =NEXT= alone.
=claude-code-ide-org--map-siblings= walks with =org-get-next-sibling= /
=org-get-previous-sibling=, which stop at the enclosing parent's
boundary, so the level scoping is structural rather than incidental. The
defect is not that the cascade reaches the wrong level — it is that at
the *right* level it never asks what kind of heading it is promoting.

*Fix is one clause*, mirroring the auto-clock-in trigger: skip the
promotion when the sole remaining TODO is a container. Open question
whether it should then promote nothing, or descend and promote the
container's own sole remaining child — the second is more useful and
more surprising, and no evidence has been gathered either way.

:END:
*Shipped 2026-08-21*, in one pass with [[id:c8a6c5d2-8777-44d2-9900-e56eb03aa2d9][c8a6c5d2]] -- two guards on one function sharing one test scaffold. =--trigger-auto-promote-sole-todo= now consults =--container-heading-p= and promotes nothing when the sole survivor is a container.

*Guarded at the promotion site, not while collecting candidates* -- the narrower of the two readings. A group of {container TODO, leaf TODO} still promotes nothing, exactly as before. Excluding containers from the *count* instead would newly promote the leaf there: more useful, possibly right, and a behaviour change this defect did not ask for.

*Descend-vs-nothing is decided in favour of nothing*, matching the honest-nil argument =--review-suggest-heading= makes for the same class of refusal at [[id:62c6b1be-4e3c-4ea1-9f0c-19ee70be0e1e][62c6b1be]]. Still no evidence either way; the test pins the shipped answer so that changing it later has to be deliberate.

*Verified by mutation, then live.* Removing the condition fails only the new container test. Applying it to *every* heading rather than containers only fails that test's discriminating partner -- the pre-existing sole-remaining-TODO promotion test -- which is the same over-application signal 62c6b1be relied on. In the running Emacs after =load-file=: a container sole survivor stays TODO with zero =Auto-promoted= lines, a leaf sole survivor comes out NEXT with one.

*Measured live 2026-08-21, at the cost of 24 minutes credited to the wrong heading.* Four spans applied at review all named [[id:420816ec-677e-45a5-b898-fb5db70d214b][420816ec]] -- 0:07, 0:03, 0:12 and 0:02 -- none of which was work on it. The 0:12 was reassigned by hand to [[id:9202b39d-49e4-441c-89f2-382feb4ef1ea][9202b39d]]; the other three are genuinely cross-cutting and were left where they landed, which is [[id:a1d63f52-4c07-4b9e-8f31-6d2b90c4e7a5][a1d63f52]]'s case arriving in practice.

*=claude-code-ide-org--review-suggest-heading= behaved exactly as documented*, and that is the point. Its rule is that a heading is the answer while it is in a work-in-progress state and nothing has taken it out. 420816ec entered DOING at [2026-08-20 Thu 21:10] and never left, so it was the only candidate and it won every span. No latch bug: zero matches for "container" anywhere in the function.

*But a container can never itself be the work.* =claude-code-ide-org--container-heading-p= returns =t= for 420816ec and =nil= for 9202b39d, checked live. This project already relies on exactly that distinction one screen away: =claude-code-ide-org--attention-headings-context= excludes DOING containers because "a container in DOING is a true and unremarkable statement about the project". Two consumers read the same state and treat it oppositely, and the suggester has the harmful half -- an unremarkable statement is the worst possible basis for a guess, because it is true for as long as any child is open.

*Proposed fix, one condition:* return nil when the active id is a container, letting the span fall to the unassigned path [[id:3d0487f4-b8f8-451c-88bf-ab537663cbd0][3d0487f4]] built for it. Nil is already this function's documented answer whenever it cannot do better, and the same argument its docstring makes twice -- that a plausible wrong id is worse than none -- applies with more force here, since a container's plausibility never expires.

*Distinct from [[id:d1cf852a-696a-4195-a4a7-039439c1f4b7][d1cf852a]]*, which proposes a hard *right edge* so guideposts after an increment provably leave the heading. That bounds a latch in time; this one says a whole class of heading should never be suggested at any time. Either alone would have prevented these four spans, which is worth knowing before both are built.

*The other half of the cause was mine and no code change fixes it.* CLAUDE.md's standing rule is to set DOING before beginning work on a tracked heading. This session closed befaed0a, ran the depth-counter verification and shipped [[id:e0904e93-b99d-44ad-b641-e3e13aced8c4][e0904e93]] while calling =org_clock_in= exactly once, at 08:31:36, five seconds before clocking out. Every guidepost was therefore unattributed and fell to the suggester. Container exclusion would have turned a confident wrong answer into an honest nil; it would not have produced the right one.

:END:
*Shipped 2026-08-21.* =claude-code-ide-org--review-suggest-heading= resolves its answer once at the end and returns nil when that id is a container, via a new =claude-code-ide-org--container-id-p=. Resolved at the end rather than inside the loop because the loop runs over every queued =todo= event and this reads a file. The helper mirrors =claude-code-ide-org--review-heading-title= -- =org-id-find= to a marker, =org-with-point-at=, release the marker -- and answers nil for an id that resolves to nothing, since a lookup failure is not evidence of container-ness and suppressing on it would lose a suggestion the human could still act on.

*Verified live against the heading that caused this, after =load-file=* -- the running Emacs held the old definition and would otherwise have answered for it. Given the real DOING event that won those four spans, 420816ec now yields nil, while the leaf 9202b39d still yields its own id from an identical event.

*Verified by mutation, not by a green suite.* Three mutations each fail: removing the condition (the pre-fix behaviour), applying it to every id rather than containers only, and inverting the helper. The second is the informative one -- it fails *six* tests, not one, because five existing suggestion tests depend on a leaf still being suggested. The new test asserts both directions in one place for the same reason: an assertion that only checks the container is refused would pass against a function that had simply stopped answering.

*What it does not fix, recorded so the split stays visible.* Container exclusion converts a confident wrong answer into an honest nil. It does not produce the right answer; only clocking in on the heading actually being worked does that, and the 24 minutes were lost because this session called =org_clock_in= once, at 08:31:36, five seconds before clocking out. The code half and the discipline half are independent, and only the code half is closed here.

*A detail worth keeping about why this was invisible for so long.* The defect needs a container to sit in DOING while a session works something else -- which is the normal state of this project, not an edge case. On the day it was found, all three DOING headings in TODO.org were containers, so the function could not have returned a right answer for any span at all. It had presumably been wrong for as long as containers have been entering DOING, and every wrong answer was one keystroke from correction at review, which is exactly why nobody caught it.

  different one, and it only bites when the capture file is =TODO.org=
  in the first place.
- A capture *with* a target failed: =target: "Clock lifecycle &
  visibility"= was refused as "neither a known =:ID:= nor a top-level
  heading in *notes.org*". The title form resolves against the capture
  file, so while that file is =notes.org= no category of =TODO.org= can
  be named at all.

*So the "org_capture cannot target a category" problem is this heading,
not a design limitation.* With the capture file pointing at =TODO.org=,
the categories *are* its top-level headings and the title form works.
The one-line fix above removes both symptoms.

*What it cost in the meantime*, worth recording because the workaround
looked reasonable each time: every heading created this session was
written by hand-inserted elisp instead, which is what left =org-id=
stale in [[id:8ddd7fa8-e847-42e9-b82c-63bbe4c11b7b][8ddd7fa8]] and what
produced the inline-keyword habit behind
[[id:cc0c17a7-a554-426d-afeb-09cbee7339f0][cc0c17a7]]. An unpersisted
=defcustom= propagated into three other headings before anyone asked
what it was actually part of.

*Persisted 2026-08-20.* One =setq= in the =after! org= block of
=~/.config/doom/config.el=, and set live in the running Emacs so the
tool works now.

*The path question is answered, and not the way the line above proposes.*
That line names =~/git/claude-code-ide-org/TODO.org=. Measured instead:
=claude-code-ide-org--tracked-files= returns
=/Users/neil.best/org/claude-code-ide-org/TODO.org=, =org-agenda-files=
holds the same, and only =file-truename= gives the =~/git/= path. Every
other part of this system therefore knows the file by the *symlink*
name, because =org-agenda-files= is built by scanning =org-directory=.
Pointing capture at the git path is precisely what would give =org-id=
two entries per id — the divergence this heading warned about, not one
to accept. Written as
=(expand-file-name "claude-code-ide-org/TODO.org" org-directory)= so it
tracks =org-directory= rather than restating it.

*The "narrow exposure" paragraph above is wrong and is corrected here.*
It says only *target-less* capture is affected. Measured 2026-08-19: a
capture carrying an explicit =target= of ="Clock lifecycle &
visibility"= was refused as "neither a known =:ID:= nor a top-level
heading in *notes.org*". A title target resolves against the capture
file, so while that file was =notes.org= no category could be named at
all. Only *:ID:* targets were unaffected — which is why the captures of
2026-08-15 all worked, and why the claim looked true.

:END:
*Verified by using it, not by reading it:*
[[id:3063c3e5-0dd0-4354-8985-271b0313c5d1][3063c3e5]] was filed with
=target: "Skill logic"= and landed as a level-2 heading under that
category. The same call shape failed the day before.

*One claim still open, deliberately.* Persistence itself is unverified:
setting the value live proves the tool, not the config. The =after! org=
block only runs at startup, and per the org-dev skill a check against a
layer that has not reloaded is indistinguishable from a passing one. The
next session verifies it for free — if capture works without anyone
setting anything, it persisted.

*Verified 2026-08-20, and the first check was not a verification.* After the user ran =doom/reload=, reading the variable showed the configured value — but a reload cannot disprove the alternative, because the live =setq= from the session that filed this heading would have survived it just as well. The discriminating test is to unset first: =(setq claude-code-ide-org-capture-file nil)=, then =(load (expand-file-name "config.el" doom-user-dir))=, then read. Result =(:before nil :after "/Users/neil.best/org/claude-code-ide-org/TODO.org")=. The config sets it.

*The symlink-versus-real-path argument recorded earlier does not hold, and nothing depends on it.* The value was set to the =~/org/= symlink path on the reasoning that =--tracked-files= and =org-agenda-files= use it. But =find-file-visit-truename= is =t= here, so Emacs resolves the symlink on open: the buffer visiting either path is one buffer, named for the truename =~/git/claude-code-ide-org/TODO.org=. Either value would have worked. Keeping the symlink form for consistency with the surrounding settings, not because it is load-bearing.

*Discovered by the same check, and separately useful:* =get-file-buffer= on the symlink path returns nil while a buffer for that file is plainly open, because it matches on =buffer-file-name= rather than the truename. Any future code that asks \"is this file already open?\" by that route will be wrong here.

[[id:47c027d2-7b5a-4de0-baf4-f992f3b814bd][47c027d2]] gave =org_capture=
an optional =target= and kept =(file <spec>)= as the fallback when it is
omitted — reasoned at the time as "the honest answer for placement
unknown," which append-at-end-of-file is, in general.

It is wrong for the file capture now points at. Appending to TODO.org
means a *level-1* heading, and this project reserves those for
categories: pure structure, no keyword, no tags, no properties, per
CLAUDE.md's "Top-level headings" rule. So every no-target capture would
produce a heading violating the convention on three counts at once, to
be refiled by hand — the manual step the tool exists to remove.

Nothing has landed wrong yet: both real captures named a target. Found
by using the tool rather than by review.

*Options, none chosen:*
- *Require =target=.* Simplest and most honest — refuse rather than
  guess. Costs the one case the fallback was for: a passing mention
  whose right home genuinely is not known.
- *Fall back to a designated category* rather than the file. Keeps
  capture always-succeeds, at the price of a setting to choose and an
  inbox-shaped thing arriving through the back door, which
  =47c027d2='s discussion rejected at the front.
- *Make the fallback file-aware*: append at top level only where that is
  meaningful, require a target where the file has the category
  convention. Most correct, least obvious, and needs a way to know which
  files have the convention.

Worth deciding alongside
[[id:bd482c92-a71a-4d7d-88df-47678ee94c79][bd482c92]], since this only
bites once the capture target is this project's own file — which is
exactly what that heading makes permanent.

*Second, smaller defect seen in the same capture:* the entry is inserted
with no blank line separating it from the preceding body text or the
following heading, unlike every hand-written heading in this file. Fixed
by hand here. Probably wants =:empty-lines-before 1= on the template.

*Correction, 2026-08-20:* the line above saying /"Nothing has landed
wrong yet: both real captures named a target"/ was true when written and
is no longer. On 2026-08-18 a no-target capture placed
[[id:b07df584-3adc-433c-ab49-e104f88aecf7][b07df584]] as a level-1
heading, and it sat unnoticed until someone went looking for it.

*But it landed in =~/org/notes.org=, not =TODO.org=*, which means it is
not quite this heading's defect. The capture file had reverted to
=org-default-notes-file= because
[[id:bd482c92-a71a-4d7d-88df-47678ee94c79][bd482c92]]'s setting was
never persisted. The level-1 fallback is still wrong for =TODO.org= and
this heading still stands — it simply has not been the thing biting.

Which sharpens the choice already listed: *require =target== would have
refused that call outright and cost nothing, since the caller did have a
category in mind and only omitted it out of habit.

:END:
*Shipped 2026-08-20* (=535c98c=), taking the first of the three options
above: refuse rather than guess. =target= is required in both layers
that matter — the schema drops =:optional= and says why, and the
function returns an =Error:= reply, so =bin/hooks/queue-append= also
drops a *deferred* capture rather than queuing one with nowhere to go.

*Urgency rose today rather than fell.* While the capture file had
reverted to =notes.org=
\([[id:bd482c92-a71a-4d7d-88df-47678ee94c79][bd482c92]]\) a target-less
capture merely went to the wrong file. Now that it points at =TODO.org=
again, the same call would create exactly the stray level-1 heading that
[[id:95087d8f-e16d-45d3-bdea-9b179dc672b4][95087d8f]]'s new check flags
and the pre-commit hook refuses — containment, not a fix.

*The cost this option was said to carry turned out not to be real.* It
was "the one case the fallback was for: a passing mention whose right
home genuinely is not known". The call that finally hit this had a
category in mind and omitted the argument out of habit, which is not
that case. If the real one ever arrives, the refusal names
=org_outline=, so the cost is one extra call rather than a wrong
placement.

*Six existing tests captured without a target and now name one*, which
meant giving the fixture a category to name — =Scratch=, because
=capture-target-by-category-title= makes its own =Tooling= and two would
not be unique on level 1. Those headings are level 2 now and the
assertions moved with them. The test that asserted the old fallback
asserts the refusal instead, across nil, empty and whitespace; removing
the guard fails it and nothing else.

Observed 2026-08-19: apply refused [[id:9651d4c8-6887-4b0a-91d9-562c3bc49a75][9651d4c8]]'s =TODO -> TODO=. There was nothing to do -- the heading already held that keyword -- but the event was queued, offered at review, marked, and failed there.

*Cause.* The heading was created by writing the keyword straight into the heading text, and =org_set_todo TODO= was then called on it. The tool recorded the transition faithfully; the reply even said =(was TODO)=, which was the signal and was not read.

*Two places it could be stopped, and they are not equivalent.* =org_set_todo= could refuse to queue when =from= equals =to=, which costs one comparison and gives the caller immediate feedback instead of a failure hours later at apply. Or apply could treat a no-op as satisfied rather than failed, since the file already holds the requested state. Doing both is defensible: refuse early, be tolerant late for events queued before the refusal existed.
:END:

*Problem.* =org_set_todo= queued transitions whose requested state was already the state on disk. Each no-op cost a queue event, a review-buffer line and a dismissal. Four occurrences in one day, all the same pattern: writing a keyword inline at heading creation -- because =org_capture= cannot target a category ([[id:97696fc2-f07b-4586-b280-de6a7d26fb87][97696fc2]]) -- then calling =org_set_todo= for that same state out of habit.

*Solution: refuse at the source; the apply side already tolerated it.* =org_set_todo= now returns an =Error:= reply when the requested state is already held on disk, so =bin/hooks/queue-append= drops the event and the no-op never reaches the queue (=c2cf203=). The =Error:= prefix is the mechanism rather than a verdict -- the hook decides by testing for it, so refusing *requires* it, and the wording carries what the prefix misstates. It compares against disk, not against pending events, which is what =from= means everywhere else. Apply needed no code change, but its tolerance is now pinned by a test rather than working by omission (=9b4d4f8=).

*Verified* end to end through the MCP tool rather than by calling the elisp -- the reply was the refusal and the queue file stayed at 121 lines. An earlier check proved nothing: invoking the function over =emacsclient= never fires the =PostToolUse= hook that writes the queue, so the count could not have moved either way.

*Falsified -- the premise this heading was filed on.* Its original title asserted such a transition "reaches apply and fails there". Probed 2026-08-20: applying a =TODO -> TODO= item returns nil, leaves the keyword untouched and writes no State line, and a queued chain (=NEXT -> DOING= then =NEXT -> DONE=, both carrying =from: NEXT=) applies in one pass. The heading was filed on an inference drawn from two failures in one apply run whose error text was never read. Retitled, because a false title is the worst stale claim: it is what a reader sees without opening the body.

*Loose end, deliberately unexplained:* what actually failed for [[id:9651d4c8-6887-4b0a-91d9-562c3bc49a75][9651d4c8]] in that run. If it fails again, the error text is the evidence this heading never had.

/This heading is the trial vehicle for the/ =:PLAN:= /drawer layout (2026-08-21), which is why its shape differs from its siblings. The planning content sits in a drawer beside/ =:PROPERTIES:= /and/ =:LOGBOOK:= /rather than below the prose, so a folded heading shows the debrief and nothing else./

One arc in three steps: find the structural drift that already exists,
teach the linter to catch that class, then stop new instances reaching
history.

The three were filed separately over two weeks and only read as a set
once =7e9aa4ea= joined them on 2026-08-19. Composed rather than left
scattered because they must land in this order — the diagnosis decides
what rules are worth writing, and enforcing rules nobody has validated
would block commits on false positives.

*Evidence from one session, 2026-08-18/19.* Five structural errors were
introduced and committed: four =:ID:= UUIDs written from memory, each
with a correct 8-character prefix and a wrong tail, and one line of
prose that wrapped so =30.= began a line and org parsed it as an
ordered-list bullet. All five were caught by =bin/lint-org= *after* the
commit, each needing a follow-up. That is the case for the third step
and it is also a rough measure of the rate.

Every member already carries its own detail; this heading deliberately
holds only what the set shares.

:END:
*All three children done, 2026-08-19.* The arc held: the diagnosis
decided what rules were worth writing, and the rules were validated
before being enforced.

- [[id:8d682a5b-1b03-4744-995c-a871a8b40ddc][8d682a5b]] — all eleven
  org-lint reports were markdown bold, none a misplaced heading. Fixing
  them took 28 warnings to 18, and had to convert twenty-one spans
  rather than the ten flagged, because org-lint only reports a closing
  marker followed by a space and the ten are entangled with the rest.
- [[id:95087d8f-e16d-45d3-bdea-9b179dc672b4][95087d8f]] — two checks org
  had no opinion on. The second needed neither design this heading
  proposed: categories identify themselves by carrying =:ARCHIVE:=.
- [[id:7e9aa4ea-4757-4e58-bac3-3c3e67fc4cb1][7e9aa4ea]] — the commit
  gate, scoped to staged content, verified by refusing a real commit.

*Ordering was load-bearing, as expected.* Had the gate landed first it
would have been enforcing rules nobody had validated, against a corpus
carrying eighteen unexamined warnings.

*Backdated into DOING* at 17:48, when 8d682a5b started, rather than at
composition — see
[[id:241a4c54-ed59-4780-b602-2a86efee978a][241a4c54]] for why that rule
is written nowhere and why writing it down is not trivial. No clock: a
container's own CLOCK line lands inside the total org already rolls up
from its children.

*Surfaced 2026-08-14 the moment =org-lint= was wired into
[[id:3bd3402b-3ab6-4ace-b20b-3ff84caa3fb2][3bd3402b]]'s script,* which
is the whole argument for having run it sooner.

=org-lint= reports "Possibly misplaced heading line" at =TODO.org= lines
3304, 3323, 4067, 4074, 4077, 4097, 4183, 6875, 7709 and 9785, and
=DONE.org= 743. None is diagnosed yet. (A twelfth report, a bullet-
counter complaint at =TODO.org= 822, is unrelated and also unexamined.)

*Why it is worth diagnosing rather than silencing.* One instance of this
exact shape was found by hand the same day: a heading glued to the end
of a prose line (=f39944f=, 2026-08-13), which org does not parse as a
heading at all — so it is invisible to =org-agenda=, =org_outline= and
every =org_*= tool, its =:ID:= is unreachable, and links to it dangle,
while the raw text still *looks* correct to a reader. If even one of
these eleven is that, a tracked heading is missing from the system
without anyone knowing.

*Expect false positives too.* The checker hedges in its own wording, and
these files quote org syntax in prose constantly — example blocks,
inline bold at line start, the transition tables. Sorting real from
quoted is the actual work, and the answer decides whether these become
errors or stay warnings.

:END:
*Diagnosed 2026-08-19. All eleven are markdown-style =**bold**= in files
whose bold is =*single*=. None is a misplaced heading.*

=org-lint-misplaced-heading= searches for =[^*\n\r ,]\*\*+ = — an
ordinary character, two or more asterisks, then a space — as a heuristic
for the corruption its own docstring illustrates:

: ** Heading 1** Oops heading 2

What it actually catches here is the *closing* =**= of a markdown bold
span followed by a space. Running that regex over both files returns
exactly eleven lines, matching the eleven reports one for one:

| file     |                                            lines |
|----------+--------------------------------------------------|
| TODO.org |                                       2505, 6304 |
| DONE.org | 3047, 3058, 3649, 3656, 3660, 3669, 3757, 6079, 9363 |

*Ten are real defects; one is not.* =DONE.org:9363= names a level-4 heading inside verbatim markup —
a true false positive. The other ten are markdown habit leaking into
org.

*And they are visible defects, not merely stylistic.* Checked in this
Emacs: org parses =**bold**= as a =bold= element whose *contents* are
the literal string =*bold*=. So it renders as bold text with stray
asterisks around it, which is not what any of the ten authors intended.

*The finding for [[id:95087d8f-e16d-45d3-bdea-9b179dc672b4][95087d8f]]*:
org-lint already detects this class — the problem is that it reports it
under a name describing a different and much more alarming defect.
Anyone reading "Possibly misplaced heading line" goes looking for broken
structure and finds prose. A local checker naming it "markdown bold in
an org file" would cost one regex and would not need org-lint's
heuristic at all.

*Not fixed here.* Ten mechanical edits collapsing a doubled asterisk
to a single one, nine of them in
=DONE.org=, would take the warning count from 28 to 18. Left as its own
decision because the spans cross line breaks in at least one case
\(TODO.org 2504-2505\) and because editing archived prose deserves to be
asked for rather than assumed.

*Fixed 2026-08-19* (=4f25341=). Warnings 28 -> 18. Twenty-one spans
converted, not ten — and that was forced rather than chosen.

*The flagged subset cannot be fixed on its own.* org-lint only reports a
closing marker followed by a space, so the ten it names are scattered
through a class of twenty-one whose members share delimiters. A first
attempt to fix only the ten matched from one span's opening across to a
later span's closing and collapsed the outer pair, leaving
=DONE.org:3051= and =3058= each with one marker of the wrong width. That
was reverted.

*What worked:* pair the markers properly. Walk every doubled asterisk
that is not inside verbatim markup and not part of a longer run;
classify as opening when the next character is not whitespace and
closing when the previous one is not; pair within a paragraph. Twenty-one
spans, each read before applying.

Left alone, correctly: glob patterns inside =paths:= values, the
verbatim mention that names the marker itself, the level-4 heading in
=DONE.org:9363=, and eight example heading lines inside fixed-width
blocks. =DONE.org= now holds no doubled asterisk outside verbatim at
all; the eight left in =TODO.org= are all examples.

*Verification worth reusing:* every changed line, with asterisks
stripped, matches its predecessor exactly — so the edit provably changed
nothing but emphasis markers. That check is what caught the corruption
the first time, and it is cheap.

- State "DONE"       from "DOING"      [2026-08-19 Wed 19:23] \\
  re-queued; prior event went stale on from
:END:
:PLAN:

Two checks =bin/lint-org= does not have, both identified 2026-08-17 after
a single line of prose re-parented 6462 lines of TODO.org and survived
two days, a full review-and-apply, and repeated clean lint runs.

*The incident, stated once so the checks have something concrete to be
tested against.* =* * *= was written into
[[id:b5f7c5c7-7ad6-4c68-9cce-3479db1f1644][b5f7c5c7]]'s closing summary
as a horizontal rule -- the markdown idiom, reached for without thinking.
In org a =*= at column 0 is a headline, so it became a *level-1 category
titled "* *"* which swallowed lines 3174--9636: sixteen level-2 headings
and the queue epic's thirty-four children, none of which belonged to it.

*=lint-org= reported =0 errors= throughout, correctly.* The file was
valid org the entire time. That is the whole point of these two checks:
the existing suite asks whether the file parses and whether this
project's conventions hold on the headings it finds, and neither question
notices a heading that should not exist at all.

*Check 1: a heading title that is punctuation only.* =* *= has no word
characters. No real heading in either file does, and none plausibly
would. Cheap, and it catches the exact shape that occurred -- at any
level, not just level 1.

*Check 2: a level-1 heading outside the file's known categories.*
Stronger and more general: level-1 headings in TODO.org are categories,
a small and slow-changing set, and one appearing mid-file is almost
certainly an accident. Would have caught this even if the phantom had
been named something word-like. Needs a decision about how the known set
is expressed -- enumerated in the check, or inferred as "every level-1
that existed at the last clean run", the latter being self-maintaining
but only as trustworthy as the run that seeded it.

*Where they go.* =claude-code-ide-org--lint-file= (config.el:5501) is
where the per-file conventions are checked; =bin/lint-org= is the 84-line
shell wrapper and needs no change. Per that script's own header, each
check wants a fixture that violates it -- "a lint whose assertions have
never been seen to fail proves nothing".

*Filed as one heading covering both* because they are one change to one
check suite, tested the same way, arising from one incident. Split them
if either turns out to want its own design decision -- check 2 plausibly
does, over how the known category set is defined.

*Related but distinct:*
[[id:8d682a5b-1b03-4744-995c-a871a8b40ddc][8d682a5b]] is about
diagnosing org-lint's *existing* misplaced-heading reports; this is about
adding checks org-lint has no opinion on.

:END:
*Shipped 2026-08-19* (=cc25adc=). Both checks live in
=claude-code-ide-org--lint-file=; =bin/lint-org= needed no change, as
predicted. Replayed against the incident by injecting =* *= into a copy
of the real =TODO.org=: each check flags it independently.

*Check 2 needed neither option this heading offered.* The choice recorded
here was an enumerated category list or a set inferred from the last
clean run. The categories already identify themselves: measured on the
real files, all seven level-1 headings in =TODO.org= carry =:ARCHIVE:=
and none of =DONE.org='s seven do, because the latter are archive
targets. So the routing set is collected across every linted file and
matched by title — a target is recognised by the source it mirrors. No
enumeration to maintain, no seed state whose trustworthiness depends on
the run that made it, and adding a category keeps the check correct for
free.

*One constraint this heading did not anticipate.* The suite's own
fixtures use a bare =* Category= with no =:ARCHIVE:=, so an
unconditional rule fails its positive control. The check is skipped when
no routing level-1 exists anywhere in the linted set: with nothing to
infer the convention from, saying nothing is the honest answer. It costs
nothing here, where seven categories route.

*Both got a violating fixture*, per this file's rule. Four mutations
checked; three discriminated at once. The fourth — removing the mirror
allowance — failed nothing, because its fixture's only level-1 carried
=:ARCHIVE:= so the allowance was never reached. Replaced with a two-file
fixture, the only shape in which a mirror exists, and it discriminates.

*And the trap documented three lines above the new function was walked
into anyway:* =org-map-entries= resolves =file= scope through
=buffer-file-name=, which a temp buffer has not got, so it maps over
nothing and reports that as success. The collector silently returned no
categories and the check silently passed. Scope nil, with the comment
repeated at the new call site.

=bin/test= 321/321; =bin/lint-org= unchanged at 0 errors / 18 warnings,
so neither check false-positives on the real corpus.

*Not split.* Both landed as one change, as this heading allowed for —
check 2's design decision resolved itself once the =:ARCHIVE:= property
turned out to be the discriminator.

=bin/lint-org= runs nowhere automatically — not in a hook, not in
=bin/test=. The only git hook is =.githooks/pre-push=, which checks the
plans archive. =core.hooksPath= is already set to =.githooks=, so a new
hook needs no setup step.

*Evidence it would pay.* Five org errors were introduced and committed
across 2026-08-18/19: four =:ID:= UUIDs written from memory (correct
8-character prefix, wrong tail, every time) and one line of prose that
wrapped so =30.= began a line, which org parsed as an ordered-list
bullet. All five were caught by =bin/lint-org= *after* the commit and
each needed a follow-up commit. Runtime is 1.6s over both files.

*Scope to staged =.org= files, linting their staged content.* The
=pre-push= hook's own header argues against pre-commit for =sync-plans=
on two grounds. Neither survives here: it would mutate the index —
linting mutates nothing; and it would couple unrelated commits — true
only of a whole-tree lint. Scoped to staged paths, an elisp-only commit
lints nothing and costs nothing, and a concurrent session's unstaged org
edit cannot block it. Linting the staged content rather than the
worktree is also the more correct semantics: the check should describe
what is about to be committed.

*Fail on errors only.* 28 warnings are currently accepted and would
block every commit.

*Why not pre-push instead*, which is where this project puts its other
check: pre-push is too late for the observed harm. All five errors were
caught before any push; the cost was noise in local history, which only
a pre-commit hook prevents. Whether pre-push should lint as well, for
anything that reached history via =--no-verify=, is open and cheap.

*Decided 2026-08-19: block the human too.* The caveat about blocking the
user on an error they did not write was raised and dismissed by them —
=git commit --no-verify= is the escape hatch, and
=.githooks/pre-push= already establishes the convention, documenting the
bypass in a header comment and printing =Skip: git push --no-verify= in
its own failure message. The new hook should print its equivalent.

Two things that decision does not cover, both worth building in:

- *The hook is not author-aware*, and cannot be. It lints staged =.org=
  content, so it blocks whoever runs =git commit= regardless of who
  introduced the error. That is the right behaviour — the committer is
  the one publishing it — but it means "block me on my errors" is really
  "block the commit on the file's errors".
- *Claude must never pass =--no-verify=.* All five errors this hook is
  being built for were Claude's, so a bypass Claude may use defeats the
  hook entirely. The escape hatch belongs to the human alone, and that
  needs to be a written rule rather than an assumption, because it costs
  nothing to type and would silently restore the status quo.

*Gotcha to document in the hook itself:* it lints the *staged* content,
not the Emacs buffer. =TODO.org= is normally open and sometimes has
unsaved changes — that is why =org_amend= has a deferred path at all —
so a clean lint at commit time says nothing about what is still only in
the buffer.

:END:
*Shipped 2026-08-19* (=4b22f72=), as =.githooks/pre-commit= with
=bin/pre-commit-test= beside it. =core.hooksPath= was already set, so it
took effect with no setup step.

*Verified live in this repo, not only in a fixture:* appending =* *= to
=TODO.org= and committing was refused, reporting both checks added that
afternoon under [[id:95087d8f-e16d-45d3-bdea-9b179dc672b4][95087d8f]],
and nothing landed. The commit that added the hook itself stages no org,
so it exited immediately — the free path, demonstrated by the change
that introduced it.

Seven tests, of which two pin the staged-versus-worktree distinction in
both directions: a clean staged file with a broken worktree passes, and a
broken staged file with a clean worktree refuses. That is the case a
worktree-based check would get backwards.

*The first draft failed every passing case.* It used =mapfile=, an
associative array, and a bare =\"${arr[@]}\"= on an empty array — all
bash 4 or later. macOS ships 3.2 and =#!/usr/bin/env bash= resolves to
it, so the refusing cases passed for the wrong reason while every
should-pass case exited 1. Rewritten for 3.2, with the constraint stated
in the hook's own header.
[[id:84b7d8b3-5161-4146-9167-0e7e2100e365][84b7d8b3]] is the standing
shell question; this is it arriving in practice, and it is evidence that
project scripts are not currently written against a stated baseline.

- State "DONE"       from "DOING"      [2026-08-19 Wed 17:47] \\
  overlap-aware apply shipped and verified

Raised by the user 2026-08-19: /"Don't we have to allow for the
possibility that users will toggle TODO status directly and expect it to
be accepted and incorporated gracefully?"/ Yes — and the honest answer
is that it half is.

*What already works, verified rather than assumed.* =TODO.org= declares
=DOING(d!)=, and the =!= cookie makes org write a timestamped line on
*every* entry to that state, hand-edits included. Probed live
2026-08-19 on a scratch file: =C-c C-t= to DOING leaves

: - State "DOING"      from "TODO"       [2026-08-19 Wed 07:28]

and no clock. (The probe needed =(run-hooks 'post-command-hook)= to see
it — org schedules the log line from =post-command-hook=, which does not
fire under =emacsclient -e=, so a first probe wrongly reported no line
at all.) The queue side is graceful too:
=claude-code-ide-org--review-state-stale-p= compares a queued event's
=from= against the file's *current* state, so a hand-edit that moves a
heading under a queued transition is detected and the replay refused
rather than silently applied.

So the *transition* is accepted, recorded, timestamped, and defended
against stale replay. Nothing is lost.

*What is not incorporated is time, and only in one case.* If the human
hand-sets DOING and then *Claude* works, guideposts produce a span and
the time is recorded through the queue. If the human hand-sets DOING and
works *alone*, there are no guideposts, no span, and — since
[[id:226ed53b-c302-4529-870f-a42962b50bde][226ed53b]]'s step 2(c) —
no trigger either. That work is timed only if they remember =C-c C-x
C-i=. Converting a discipline requirement back into a mechanism is
exactly what this project normally does.

*Why simply re-enabling the trigger is not the fix.* The original defect
behind 226ed53b was not "a clock exists outside the queue" — a human's
own bare CLOCK line is legitimate and expected
([[id:4f8500e6-b468-4fd4-a0f6-ebf04c7a57ba][4f8500e6]]). It was *double
counting*: =38b92521='s drawer claimed 3:59 for a session spanning 3:22,
because a trigger-opened clock and a queue-derived span covered the same
period on the same heading. That happens whenever both mechanisms are
live at once, which is precisely the case the user is asking about.

*The enabling fix is the third direction 226ed53b listed and never
took*: have apply refuse to write a run that overlaps an existing CLOCK
line on the same heading. With that in place the trigger can be switched
back on — or even defaulted back on — because the failure it caused
becomes unreachable.

Note this corrects a claim written into 226ed53b on 2026-08-18, which
called that direction moot on the grounds that "apply no longer writes a
span end to end, so there is no long interval left to overlap with".
Wrong: 2(b) makes the written lines *shorter*, not non-overlapping. A
human clocking 10:00–11:00 by hand while Claude works 10:20–10:40 still
yields 80 minutes of CLOCK for 60 minutes elapsed.

*The deeper reason it bites, worth stating once.*
[[id:b8e6007a-ae13-4b13-bb2e-a5df39435af0][b8e6007a]] separated the two
quantities *semantically* — the agenda answers "where did my attention
go", the queue answers "what was the agent doing", and the annotation
style distinguishes them. But both still write =CLOCK:= lines into the
same drawer, and =org-clock-sum= and every clocktable add them up
identically. The separation exists in the annotations and not in the
arithmetic, so any report double counts wherever the two overlap. That
is the same shape as
[[id:7d739afd-f879-445c-b0b6-65e295585a94][7d739afd]]'s union rule, one
level up: there it was two agent sessions, here it is the agent and the
human.

*Not decided:* whether apply should skip an overlapping run, trim it to
the uncovered remainder, or write it and report the overlap for a human
to resolve. Trimming is the most accurate and the most likely to
surprise; skipping is the most conservative and loses agent time the
human's clock did not really represent.

*The NEXT cascade is intact on hand-edits, and that was worth checking
rather than assuming.* Raised by the user as the special case: toggling
TODO or MAYBE to NEXT should set off side effects. It does. Probed live
2026-08-19 on a scratch file with three siblings — one already =NEXT=,
one =MAYBE=, one =TODO= — and hand-setting the =MAYBE= one to =NEXT=
produced:

: ** TODO Already the next action
:   Auto-demoted: superseded by sibling [[id:probe-maybe][Someday item]] becoming NEXT.
: ** NEXT Someday item
: ** TODO A third one

So GTD's single-next-action-per-group is enforced, the demotion is
explained in place, and the superseding sibling is named by an
=[[id:]]= link rather than a title that could later go stale.

The reason this survives is structural rather than lucky:
=claude-code-ide-org-auto-clock-in-on-doing= gates *only*
=--trigger-auto-clock-in=. =--trigger-demote-conflicting-next= and
=--trigger-auto-promote-sole-todo= are registered on =org-trigger-hook=
alongside it and read no flag at all, so 2(c) narrowed exactly one
behaviour and left the cascade untouched. Confirmed by grep: the flag
has one reader in the whole file.

*Which sharpens what this heading is actually about.* Of the things a
hand-edit could reasonably expect —

| the transition is applied                    | works |
| it is timestamped in the log                 | works |
| a stale queued event cannot silently replay over it | works |
| the NEXT cascade fires                       | works |
| the work gets timed                          | *does not* |

— only the last is missing, and only when the human then works alone.
Everything else already behaves the way the user's question assumes it
should. That narrows the fix to the overlap question above rather than
to anything about how transitions are accepted.

:END:
*Shipped 2026-08-19* (=eca3a77=). Apply subtracts the heading's
already-recorded CLOCK intervals from each run before writing, so a hand
clock and a reconstructed span compose instead of summing. With that in
place =claude-code-ide-org-auto-clock-in-on-doing= is back on by
default, so a hand-set DOING times itself again.

*Subtract, not skip.* Skipping a run that overlaps would discard real
agent time falling outside the human's clock — the undercount
[[id:7d739afd-f879-445c-b0b6-65e295585a94][7d739afd]]'s rule rejects in
the other direction. A run straddling a recorded interval comes back as
the two pieces outside it.

=--logbook-has-interval-p= is removed, subsumed: a replay finds its own
previous line among the recorded intervals and subtracts to nothing. The
old check only recognised an interval written verbatim, so a re-derived
run whose endpoints moved by a second went straight past it.

*Two subtleties the tests caught, not review.* The envelope annotation
had to be gated on what was *observed* rather than what survives
subtraction — keyed on the latter a replay writes one annotation
spanning every run, a line no first pass produces. And subtraction must
only filter runs it actually cut; filtering unconditionally swallowed
the zero-width span's annotation, which reaches the writer intact
precisely so it can be annotated without a CLOCK line.

*Verified:* =bin/test= 318/318, three mutations each failing the test
that pins them. Confirmed live — =C-c C-t= to DOING opened a clock on
that heading. Note the flag needed =custom-reevaluate-setting= in the
running Emacs: =defcustom= does not reset an already-bound variable, so
the new default reaches an existing session only when set explicitly,
and otherwise at next start.

*Still open from this heading:* nothing about hand-set transitions. The
gap it named — a heading hand-set to DOING and worked alone going
untimed — is closed by the trigger being back on.

Raised by the user 2026-08-12: nothing has been archived in quite some
time, and *certainly not since the queue cutover*. So the open question
about whether this file's hierarchy earns its keep — the user floated
flattening the source instead — should be judged on what a real archive
pass actually does, not on inference. Blocked on
[[id:b5f7c5c7-7ad6-4c68-9cce-3479db1f1644][b5f7c5c7]] deliberately: that
epic's children are most of the current DONE backlog, and archiving it
mid-flight would scatter an epic still being worked.

*What is already known going in, verified 2026-08-12 rather than
assumed:*

- =org-archive-save-context-info= includes =olpath= and *is* writing it —
  18 of DONE.org's 22 archived headings carry =:ARCHIVE_OLPATH:=. The
  outline path survives archiving. An earlier claim in
  [[id:cce72644-7d5e-4def-a165-0a3b815f482b][cce72644]] that archiving
  loses structure was wrong and has been corrected there; the section
  that vanished was removed by hand in =b716d37=, not by archiving.
- DONE.org is *not* in =claude-code-ide-org--tracked-files=, which
  returns only TODO.org and =~/org/notes.org=. So =org_query= and an
  unscoped =org_clock_report= do not see archived work at all — which is
  its own question once a large archive pass moves a lot of history out
  of view. Related: the still-MAYBE "Consider archives in
  org_clock_report's scope (agenda-with-archives)".
- But =org-id-find= *does* resolve into DONE.org — an archived
  heading's =:ID:= still resolves. Confirmed on =405e05b6=.

*The risk that asymmetry creates, and the reason this is worth a
deliberate pass rather than a bulk action.* The review buffer resolves
headings with =org-id-find= (=--review-current-state=). So a heading
archived while it still has *unapplied queued events* would later have
those events applied straight into DONE.org. That is arguably correct —
the record follows the heading — but it is untested, and post-cutover
the queue routinely holds unapplied events for exactly the headings most
likely to be archived, since a heading reaches DONE by way of a queued
transition. *Empty the review buffer first, then archive*, and confirm
the behavior deliberately instead of discovering it.

*That precondition originally read "drain the queue first," which is
unsatisfiable as literally stated* — corrected 2026-08-12 on measuring
it. A queue file never reaches all-events-applied: only events that
become *items* are ever marked, and =clock_in=/=clock_out= plus
unclustered =pause=/=resume= guideposts never do. Measured that day,
with the review buffer reporting "Nothing pending": =todo= 31 of 31
consumed — every state transition ever queued — against 14 =clock_in=,
17 =clock_out=, 109 =pause= and 113 =resume= residual, 253 events in
all. The achievable, and sufficient, precondition is *the review buffer
proposes nothing*, since an event that yields no item cannot be applied
into DONE.org either. See
[[id:78f485a8-e808-43ce-af5f-277a5c97c471][78f485a8]], which owns the
file-lifecycle half of this.

*Then make the judgment.* With a real pass to look at: does the
remaining hierarchy in TODO.org still earn its keep, or should the
source be flattened further? Note =b716d37= already flattened one level
by hand on 2026-08-04, collapsing =* Roadmap / ** Section / *** Task=
into =* Section / ** Task=, so this would be the second such pass rather
than the first — and the top level is load-bearing for CLAUDE.md's
"top-level headings are categories" convention.

*DONE.org's flat =* Done= is a choice, not a constraint — and the
alternative works.* The user, 2026-08-12: the
=#+ARCHIVE: DONE.org::* Done= line is what
produced that single top-level heading; they did not care for it when
they set it up but let it ride. *Hot-take preference: mirror TODO.org's
top-level heading instead*, so archived work lands under
=* Skill logic=, =* Tooling=, and so on.

*It can be expressed, and was verified end-to-end 2026-08-12* against a
scratch file, not inferred from the docstring alone.

*The wrong lever is =%s=.* In the headline half of an archive location
it substitutes the *file name*, not the outline path — =::* From %s=
yields "From TODO.org". No amount of =#+ARCHIVE:= alone can mirror a
source heading.

*The right lever is an inherited =:ARCHIVE:= property.* Per
=org-archive-location='s own docstring it is honoured "if found in the
file or in an entry, *and anywhere up the hierarchy*." With
=:ARCHIVE: DONE.org::* Skill logic= on the category heading:

| source                                     | landed under                |
|--------------------------------------------+-----------------------------|
| =* Skill logic= → task A, *and* a level-3 A2 | =* Skill logic=, created  |
| =* Tooling= → task B                       | =* Tooling=, created        |
| =* No property here= → task C              | =* Done=, via =#+ARCHIVE:=  |

Four observed properties, each of which matters to the decision:

1. *Inheritance reaches arbitrarily deep.* A level-3 heading routed
   correctly from a property on its level-1 grandparent — so one
   property per category covers every task beneath it, including
   [[id:b5f7c5c7-7ad6-4c68-9cce-3479db1f1644][b5f7c5c7]]'s twenty-odd
   children.
2. *Target headings are created on demand*, so DONE.org needs no
   pre-building.
3. *=#+ARCHIVE:= still serves as the fallback* for anything not under a
   property-bearing category — adoption can be incremental rather than
   all-at-once.
4. *Depth is flattened within a category.* The level-3 entry landed at
   level 2, a sibling of its former parent. =:ARCHIVE_OLPATH:= records
   the real parentage (=Skill logic/task A=), so it is recoverable but
   not structural. Top-level mirroring survives; sub-nesting does not.

*The cost, and it is the second instance today of the same conflict.*
This requires a =:PROPERTIES:= drawer on top-level headings, which
CLAUDE.md forbids. The same rule blocked =:LOG_INTO_DRAWER:= earlier the
same day, which is why that fix went to =#+STARTUP:= instead.

*Argument for treating =:ARCHIVE:= as an exception rather than a
violation:* the rule's stated purpose is that categories are "pure
structure — grouping related tasks," and its concrete targets are
=:ID:= and =:CREATED:=, both *task* metadata whose presence would make a
category look like work. =:ARCHIVE:= is the opposite — structural
metadata about the grouping itself, saying where its contents go.
Narrowing the rule to "no *task* metadata" rather than "no properties"
would permit this without weakening what it was written to prevent.
That wording change belongs to
[[id:02aaae22-0958-4c0f-b5bb-2cbea32416ae][02aaae22]] if adopted.

*One thing to decide in the same breath:* the existing 22 archived
headings all sit under =* Done=. Adopting mirroring leaves a split
archive unless DONE.org is reorganised retroactively — which is
mechanical rather than a judgement call, since every entry already
carries an =:ARCHIVE_OLPATH:= naming its source category.

-----

*The structure question, judged 2026-08-17 — the second half of this
heading.* Keep the hierarchy. Keep the categories. Rebalance nothing.

*The premise largely dissolved rather than being answered.* This was raised
because TODO.org was unwieldy at 12,927 lines. It is 4,645 now, and 84% of
what remains is live work rather than finished work. That is a legitimate
outcome for a question deliberately deferred until there was evidence: the
pass was supposed to inform the judgement, and what it showed is that the
pressure motivating it is mostly gone.

*Depth stays.* Eight level-3 children remain, seven of them under one
heading, against 34 that archived today. Vestigial by count — but the count
is low *because archiving works*: epics finish and leave. Removing the
capability because it is currently underused would delete a mechanism
several shipped features depend on, notably
=claude-code-ide-org--container-heading-p= and the auto-clock-in exemption
[[id:ab75d6d2-0e59-405d-92c6-2c67488db133][ab75d6d2]] built on it, and
would forbid outright what
[[id:b5f94b88-76e3-4a3c-ac73-729f34d33691][b5f94b88]] argues should be
allowed to emerge.

*Categories stay, and flattening them got more expensive today.* The
original hot take was to flatten the source. DONE.org's mirroring now
depends on level-1 headings carrying =:ARCHIVE:=; remove the categories and
archive routing dies, back to a flat =* Done= or a new mechanism. Worth
recording for whoever asks again: the answer to this question changed as a
side effect of the same pass that was meant to inform it.

*Imbalance measured and accepted, not fixed.*

| category                     | tasks | children | lines |
|------------------------------+-------+----------+-------|
| Clock lifecycle & visibility |    18 |        7 |  2011 |
| Tooling                      |    10 |        0 |   936 |
| Skill logic                  |     8 |        0 |   707 |
| Observability                |     6 |        0 |   667 |
| Bigger swings                |     4 |        0 |   327 |
| Documentation                |     2 |        0 |   101 |
| Upstream (claude-code-ide.el)|     1 |        1 |    41 |

Clock lifecycle is 43% of the file. Splitting it was considered and
rejected: the imbalance reflects where the work has been for two weeks, not
bad structure, and equalising line counts optimises the wrong thing. It
would also cost a rename of a category's =:ARCHIVE:= and its DONE.org
heading in the same edit, which is the silent-duplicate hazard now
documented in =.claude/rules/org-conventions.md=.

*One convention tightened in the same breath, from the user:* a child
should not be archived directly *unless it is being promoted to a sibling
explicitly in the same move*. The earlier wording here was a blanket
"archive at level 2 only", which forbade a legitimate deliberate act along
with the accidental one. Recorded in =org-conventions.md=.

*Reopened as a question, not as work -- the reason recorded here for closing the flattening half is weaker than it looked.* Measured 2026-08-21: an archived subtree carries =:ARCHIVE_CATEGORY:= automatically, alongside =:ARCHIVE_FILE:=, =:ARCHIVE_TODO:=, =:ARCHIVE_TIME:= and =:ARCHIVE_OLPATH:=. So flattening the level-1 categories does not lose the category at all -- org demotes it to a property, which is queryable and column-viewable where a heading level is not. "Archive routing depends on level-1 =:ARCHIVE:=" is a routing question, and routing is the thing flattening deliberately gives up in exchange for a chronological record.

Left DONE: the archiving this heading actually did is done, and the structure question it deferred now lives at [[id:29439196-bbb8-4b64-b8d5-3bf9d457bf6c][29439196]], promoted to TODO the same day on separate evidence.
