Raised by the user 2026-08-12, on moving
[[id:b5f7c5c7-7ad6-4c68-9cce-3479db1f1644][b5f7c5c7]] to =DOING= because
some of its children had become active — which is the right thing to
express, and should happen whenever a child goes active. The problem is
what came with it: =claude-code-ide-org--trigger-auto-clock-in= fires on
*any* transition to =DOING=/=PLANNING=, hand-edits explicitly included,
so the toggle also opened a clock on the epic. That interval was
unwanted and was deleted by hand.

*Org already does the roll-up, natively.* Measured on this very epic
before the deletion — the clocktable read =14:52= for the parent row,
the ten children summed to =13:44=, and the =1:08= difference is exactly
the epic's own two CLOCK lines. So "activity rolls up to the parent in
reporting" needs no configuration; it is what =:maxlevel= does. The
consequence is the actual argument: a parent's own time is *additive,
inside the same total*, so it cannot be told apart from the children's
sum once rolled up. Clocking a container does not produce a roll-up — it
adds a second, differently-meaning quantity to one that already existed.

*The counter-precedent, and why it does not transfer.* norang's org-GTD
setup ([[https://doc.norang.ca/org-mode.html]]) deliberately puts time on
projects: clocking out of a subtask *cascades up* to the parent so
unattributable time lands somewhere. Two differences. It is a *move* of
one running clock, never a second one minted alongside the children's.
And it exists to catch time no subtask claims — a problem this design
already answers elsewhere, since every interval is attributed to the
heading a session named and unattributed guideposts have
[[id:3d0487f4-b8f8-451c-88bf-ab537663cbd0][3d0487f4]].

*Proposed rule, narrower than "never clock a parent."* Parent clocking
should be *deliberate, never automatic*. The epic's existing =1:08= is
real epic-level work — planning on 08-06, revising the plan against what
shipped on 08-11 — and a blanket "only clock leaves" would discard that
category. So: exempt container headings from the auto-clock-in trigger,
and leave manual =org_clock_in= on a parent available for genuine
coordination work.

*Detecting a container, org-natively:* norang's lazy definition — a
heading with at least one child carrying a TODO keyword. No new
property, no list to maintain.

*Consequence for CLAUDE.md:* "any transition *to* =DOING= or =PLANNING=
must open a clock" acquires a stated exception, which belongs with
[[id:02aaae22-0958-4c0f-b5bb-2cbea32416ae][02aaae22]]'s rewrite rather
than as a separate edit.

*Two things observed while diagnosing this, both worth their own
attention and neither fixed here:*

1. *Deleting the open CLOCK line desynced the live clock* —
   =org-clock-marker= slid onto the *next*, already-closed line
   (=[2026-08-11 Tue 11:10]--[11:13] =>  0:03=), while =org-clocking-p=
   stayed =t=. Any subsequent =org-clock-out= — Emacs quit and suspend
   both run one — would have closed a clock at that marker and corrupted
   a good interval. Note =org-clock-cancel= is *not* the recovery: it
   deletes a region relative to that same wrong marker. Cleared by
   resetting =org-clock-marker=/=org-clock-hd-marker= in place, touching
   no file. This is
   [[id:53b0047d-c55c-486c-8eed-ba4994d97a1a][53b0047d]] observed live,
   and evidence it is not merely theoretical.
2. *=org-log-into-drawer= is nil*, so org's native state-change logging
   lands *outside* =:LOGBOOK:= — visible on b5f7c5c7, whose =DOING= note
   sits above the drawer while older entries sit inside it. Applied
   transitions do land inside, so the two paths disagree. Relevant
   because native logging working correctly is the entire premise of the
   apply design.

   *Resolved 2026-08-12, elsewhere.* Fixed by adding =#+STARTUP:
   logdrawer= to =TODO.org= and =DONE.org=, which sets the variable
   buffer-locally and leaves a user's other org files alone. The
   documentation half belongs to
   [[id:02aaae22-0958-4c0f-b5bb-2cbea32416ae][02aaae22]], with drift #4,
   since it is the same header block; the "what may a module change on
   someone else's machine" question it opened is
   [[id:1caed585-3209-4108-8501-eba16baf6a01][1caed585]]. Left recorded
   here because this is where it was found, not because this heading
   owns it.

*A third consequence, found 2026-08-14 while designing something else.*
[[id:b5f7c5c7-7ad6-4c68-9cce-3479db1f1644][b5f7c5c7]] has been =DOING=
since =[2026-08-06 Thu 22:35]= — eight days — with no clock running. In
that whole time *no session-start report has ever mentioned it*, because
=claude-code-ide-org--wait-headings-context= reports only the currently
clocked heading plus =WAIT= headings.

This surfaced while considering adding =DOING= to that report's keyword set, so
a new session would be told about headings left mid-flight. Simulated against
the real files, the proposal produced four lines where today there is one — and
three of the four are currently invisible: two leaves abandoned that morning
([[id:5ff5a4b8-2fee-472a-b5e1-c9de8cf96704][5ff5a4b8]] and [[id:4f9e552a-e1a9-48dd-8801-3f23a31b9e32][4f9e552a]]), and this epic, which would then appear in *every*
session-start report, unchanged, indefinitely.

*The finding is that the two are the same keyword and opposite news.* A
container in =DOING= is a true and unremarkable statement about the
project. A leaf in =DOING= with no clock is an increment somebody walked
away from. Only the second is worth telling a new session, and a report
that always carries the same line stops being read at all — the same
failure that
[[id:5ff5a4b8-2fee-472a-b5e1-c9de8cf96704][5ff5a4b8]]'s outcome note
records for evidence lines, which were applied without evaluation
precisely because they were always plausible.

*So the report change is downstream of this heading, not independent of
it.* If containers stopped carrying a work-in-progress keyword — or if
the container test proposed above existed anywhere reusable — the report
would need no filter at all: adding =DOING= to its keyword set would
simply do the right thing. Building the filter first would work around
the problem this heading exists to remove, and would leave two
definitions of "container" to keep in step, which is the shape of bug
this project keeps finding (see the six-keyword denylist retired from
=--review-suggest-heading= on 2026-08-14 for the same reason).

*Not the earlier symptom recurring.* The epic's clock is *closed*; this
is not the auto-clock-in trigger minting an unwanted interval again. It
is the same root — a container carrying a keyword that asserts work is
in progress — showing a second, quieter symptom eight days later. The
first cost an interval that had to be deleted by hand; this one costs
nothing visible, which is why it went unnoticed for eight days.

*And it does not affect span attribution,* which is worth stating so a
future reader does not assume it does:
=claude-code-ide-org--review-suggest-heading= derives its guess from
queued =todo= events, never from the state on disk, so an epic sitting
in =DOING= in the file is not a latch target.

*Scale, measured 2026-08-14:* 37 direct children, 10 of them still open.
The "ten children" in the clocktable measurement above was that day's
count; ten is now the number that are unfinished.

*Outcome, 2026-08-14.* Shipped as proposed, with no design changes.
=claude-code-ide-org--container-heading-p= implements norang's lazy
definition directly — scan the subtree, non-nil on the first descendant
carrying a TODO keyword — and
=claude-code-ide-org--trigger-auto-clock-in= gains it as a third guard
beside the existing re-entrancy and already-clocked-here checks. No new
property, no list to maintain, and the exemption covers =PLANNING= as
well as =DOING= since both run through that one trigger.

*Verified.* Five new tests (248 total, all green), each confirmed to
discriminate by mutating the source in two directions rather than by
passing once: forcing the guard to =t= failed exactly the two skip tests
and left the "still clocks a heading with a plain child" test passing;
deleting the keyword check from the predicate inverted that precisely —
the two skip tests passed while the predicate test and the plain-child
test failed. Then reloaded into the live Emacs and run against the real
files, where the predicate answers =t= for
[[id:b5f7c5c7-7ad6-4c68-9cce-3479db1f1644][b5f7c5c7]] and =nil= for both
[[id:4f9e552a-e1a9-48dd-8801-3f23a31b9e32][4f9e552a]] and this heading.

*One thing the heading assumed that is no longer true, and it narrows
the fix.* =--review-apply-item= binds
=claude-code-ide-org--auto-clock-in-active= for its whole duration, so
apply never reaches this trigger at all. A hand-edit in Emacs is now the
*only* path that does. That does not weaken the fix — the 2026-08-12
incident that prompted this heading was a hand-toggle, which is exactly
the surviving case — but "fires on *any* transition" above should be
read as "any transition outside apply."

=CLAUDE.md= deliberately untouched: this heading routes that edit
through [[id:02aaae22-0958-4c0f-b5bb-2cbea32416ae][02aaae22]]'s rewrite,
which already records the exception in its own scope notes.

*What this unblocks, and it is the obvious next move rather than part of
this heading:* the container test now exists somewhere reusable, which
is the precondition the "report change is downstream" section above set.
Adding =DOING= to =--wait-headings-context='s keyword set and filtering
containers through this predicate would now do the right thing, with one
definition of "container" rather than two.



**** DONE emacs is a shell function that silently breaks inline batch verification :code:
CLOSED: [2026-08-14 Fri 12:17]
:PROPERTIES:
:CATEGORY: Dev
:ID:       4f9e552a-e1a9-48dd-8801-3f23a31b9e32
:CREATED:  [2026-08-11 Tue 15:52]
:ARCHIVE_TIME: 2026-08-17 Mon 17:13
:ARCHIVE_FILE: ~/git/claude-code-ide-org/TODO.org
:ARCHIVE_OLPATH: Tooling
:ARCHIVE_CATEGORY: TODO
:ARCHIVE_TODO: DONE
:END:
:LOGBOOK:
- State "DOING"      from "TODO"       [2026-08-14 Fri 08:57] \\
  adding the skill line it proposes
CLOCK: [2026-08-14 Fri 09:09]--[2026-08-14 Fri 09:10] =>  0:01
- [2026-08-14 Fri 09:09]--[2026-08-14 Fri 09:10] task definition
CLOCK: [2026-08-14 Fri 09:22]--[2026-08-14 Fri 09:25] =>  0:03
- [2026-08-14 Fri 09:22]--[2026-08-14 Fri 09:25] task definition
CLOCK: [2026-08-14 Fri 09:30]--[2026-08-14 Fri 09:33] =>  0:03
- [2026-08-14 Fri 09:30]--[2026-08-14 Fri 09:33] task definition
CLOCK: [2026-08-14 Fri 09:37]--[2026-08-14 Fri 09:42] =>  0:05
- [2026-08-14 Fri 09:37]--[2026-08-14 Fri 09:42] task definition
- State "TODO"       from "DOING"      [2026-08-14 Fri 12:04]
- State "DONE"       from "TODO"       [2026-08-14 Fri 12:17] \\
  retcon: shipped 08-14, outcome note added
:END:

The user's shell profile defines:

: emacs () { if [[ "$*" == *-nw* ]]; then command emacs "$@"; else open -a Emacs --args "$@"; fi }

Any =emacs --batch ...= run from an interactive-profile shell therefore
launches the GUI app and returns immediately: exit 0, no stdout, no
stderr. Indistinguishable from a clean run that found nothing. Hit three
times in a row on 2026-08-11 before being noticed, and nearly recorded
as a genuine "org logs nothing" finding.

=bin/test= is unaffected — a =#!/usr/bin/env bash= script gets a
non-interactive shell where the function is not defined, so =exec emacs=
resolves to =/opt/homebrew/bin/emacs=. The trap is specific to inline
one-off verification, which is exactly where the CLAUDE.md rule about
stating the reload precondition is meant to apply.

Fix is a convention, not code: use =command emacs= or the absolute path
for any batch invocation. Worth a line in the org-dev skill, which
exists for exactly this class of "did the change take effect" check.

*Narrowed 2026-08-14: the environment half of this is not this project's
to own, and now lives in
[[id:52ede10e-5e6f-4392-b31d-b9ce9b450c3c][52ede10e]] in
=~/org/notes.org=.*

What stays here, because it impinges directly on this repo:

- =emacs --batch= run inline from a session in this repo does nothing and
  reports success, so any =check-parens=, byte-compile or =--eval= probe
  is vacuous. Recurred twice on 2026-08-14 — two paren checks, one after
  a large =config.el= edit and one after a hand-resolved merge conflict,
  both believed and both worthless.
- The convention: =command emacs= or an absolute path, never the bare
  name.
- The org-dev skill now carries that warning under its section 0
  (=d34c809=), which is what this heading originally proposed and what
  makes the rule fire at the moment of the mistake rather than sitting in
  a backlog.
- =bin/test= says =exec command emacs=. It was already safe — a
  =#!/usr/bin/env bash= script gets a non-interactive shell where no such
  function is defined — but a script in the repo that documents this
  hazard should not itself read as if unaware of it.

What moved out: the shell configuration itself — three copies of the
function across zsh and fish, one of them permanently shadowed and
unreachable; the migration to =emacsclient=-based =e=/=et= aliases;
=$EDITOR=; and a plaintext credential found in =config.fish= while
looking. *The two halves fix different things and neither replaces the
other:* deleting the function fixes one machine, while the convention and
the skill line protect any machine this project is ever installed on,
including one whose shell nobody here controls.

*One finding from the split is worth keeping on this side,* because it
explains why the bug was hard to see: fish is the login shell, but a
Claude Code Bash call runs *zsh* (=SHELL=/bin/zsh=, and the shell
snapshot it replays is a zsh snapshot). So the copy that breaks this
project's verification is the =~/.zshrc= one, and someone reasoning from
"my shell is fish" would look in the wrong file.

The split also prompted naming a goal that had never been written down —
applying these org conventions at the user level, across projects rather than
inside one repo — recorded as
[[id:9ae4b17e-278c-482f-9114-df28b2254806][9ae4b17e]] (originally
=ae2d9b4a= in =notes.org=, merged here 2026-08-15).

*Outcome, 2026-08-14.* Three artifacts, each confirmed present on disk
rather than recalled: the org-dev skill carries the warning as its own
section heading, "Never invoke bare =emacs= for a batch check — use
=command emacs=" (=d34c809=); =bin/test= says =exec command emacs=, with
a comment explaining that it was already safe and says so anyway
(=ca5d96c=); and the environment half is filed as
[[id:52ede10e-5e6f-4392-b31d-b9ce9b450c3c][52ede10e]] in =~/org/notes.org=,
still open there and deliberately not tracked from here.

*How it was verified, stated plainly because it is weaker than a test.*
The deliverable is a convention plus a line of documentation, so there is
no mechanical surface to assert against — the check was reading the three
artifacts, not running anything. Whether the skill line actually fires at
the moment of the mistake is trigger-matching against a skill
description, which this project's engineering-practices rule names as
inherently fuzzy and not worth forcing into a deterministic test. The
honest evidence is negative and thin: no bare =emacs --batch= has
recurred since the skill line landed at 08:58, against two recurrences in
the hours before it.

*Why this heading's =:LOGBOOK:= reads oddly, recorded so it is not
re-diagnosed later.* It was demoted =DOING= -> =TODO= by hand at 12:04
and closed to =DONE= shortly after, which looks like work that started
and stopped. It did not. The 09:09--09:42 span was re-annotated *task
definition* at review, and the commit record agrees: =d34c809= landed at
08:58, twelve minutes after the =DOING= transition and *before* that span
opened. The implementation was the twelve minutes; the span that looks
like it was the narrowing.

*Promoted out of [[id:b5f7c5c7-7ad6-4c68-9cce-3479db1f1644][b5f7c5c7]]
on 2026-08-13.* A capability that epic *enables* rather than one it
requires — the queue and review loop are complete without it. Filed
there only because that is where the idea surfaced, which is proximity
rather than membership.

*Prototyped by hand before being proposed, 2026-08-13*, which is why it
is filed with a recommendation rather than a question. Asked how to
identify what an unattributed span was circling, the answer that worked
was neither a transcript nor a model: *git commits and =:CREATED:=
stamps falling inside the span's own window.* Three shell commands
resolved three of four spans unambiguously.

The two strongest signals, and they differ:
- A =:CREATED:= stamp *inside* the span is the best evidence there is —
  a heading written during that time names what was being thought about.
  The 15:30--15:34 span brackets a heading created 15:33.
- A commit *just after* the span is next best, since work precedes its
  commit. That same span is followed by a commit at 15:34.

Note the asymmetry: a commit timestamp marks when work was *finished*,
not when it happened, so it anchors a span rather than bounding one. A
4-minute span preceded its commit by seconds; a 23-minute span contained
three.

*The proposal:* render each unassigned span in the review buffer
alongside the commits and headings created in its window. Nothing more —
the human still decides. Assignment stops requiring a separate =git log=
by hand, which is what it required 23 times in one sitting.

*Why this rather than
[[id:0c8644ff-f7b1-4789-ac1e-babf2e9fbc8e][0c8644ff]], and why it is that
heading's sibling rather than its child.* =0c8644ff= is specifically
"ask Claude", and carries three transport blockers plus an anchoring
objection: a fluent recommendation is harder to reject than a
transparently mechanical one, which erodes the safety property review
exists to provide. This proposal inherits none of it. No sampling, so
the transport question is moot; no transcript, so that scope question
does not arise; and it presents *evidence* rather than a recommendation,
so there is nothing to anchor on.

It is therefore not a part of =0c8644ff= but the thing to build instead,
and first — building it is what narrows =0c8644ff= to its actual
residue: spans straddling two tasks, where commits exist on both sides
and only a narrative says where the boundary fell.

*A structural reason for sibling too, worth stating because it is a
convention rather than an accident:* =TODO.org= has exactly three
heading levels — category, task, epic-child — and *zero* level-4
headings across 99 of them. A child here would introduce a fourth level
for one heading.

*Scope notes for whoever builds it.* The git query wants the repository
containing the tracked files, not =default-directory=, which at review
time is wherever the human happens to be. Heading creations are cheap to
find without scanning — =:CREATED:= is a property, so =org-map-entries=
with a property match does it. And the window should probably extend a
few minutes past the span's end to catch the commit that concluded it,
which is the asymmetry noted above.

*Outcome, 2026-08-13/14.* Shipped: an unassigned span in the review
buffer renders the git commits and =:CREATED:= stamps falling inside its
own window, interleaved chronologically. The window extends past the
span's end but never before its start, and the git query runs against the
repository containing the tracked files, found by truename so the
=~/org= symlink resolves. Memoized per window, since the render runs on
every mark keystroke. 9 ERT tests, discrimination checked by reverting
the render hook and the error guard separately.

*First real use, 2026-08-14, and it falsified the premise the feature was
built on.* Asked whether the evidence helped, the user answered: "frankly
I did not evaluate critically, everything looked reasonable." The batch
was applied without the lines being weighed.

That is exactly the anchoring objection recorded against
[[id:0c8644ff-f7b1-4789-ac1e-babf2e9fbc8e][0c8644ff]] — a fluent
recommendation is harder to reject than a transparently mechanical one —
arriving by a route this heading explicitly claimed to escape. The
argument above for building this *instead* of =0c8644ff= was that it
"presents *evidence* rather than a recommendation, so there is nothing to
anchor on." Tried once, that claim did not hold. Supporting detail makes
a suggestion easier to accept whether or not it is phrased as a
recommendation.

*A second finding, about how the report itself arrived.* The first
version of the feedback was that the commit lines needed timestamps —
which they already had, in the first column. Rendering the actual output
and putting it in front of the user resolved it: "I see them now; I may
have misremembered." Worth recording because acting on the literal
request would have added timestamps that already existed and left the
real problem untouched. Reconstructing the artifact rather than trusting
either party's recollection is what made the difference, which is the
same lesson as the standing rule about preferring the primary artifact.

*The response: report absences, not only support.* Stretches of a span
with no evidence in them are now rendered as gaps, above
=claude-code-ide-org-span-evidence-gap= (default 5 minutes, measured
against the span and never the slack window). The intent is rhetorical
rather than informational — a commit list says "here is support for the
suggestion", while a gap says "here is what you still have to decide",
which is the posture review is supposed to have.

The case that matters most is the empty one. A span with no evidence used
to render *no lines at all*, making "nothing was found here" visually
identical to "nobody looked". It now reads
=(nothing for 40m, 02:00-02:40)=. Verified live on 2026-08-14 against a
real span and a fabricated overnight one; 4 further tests, each confirmed
to fail by mutation (gaps suppressed, gaps measured against the slack
window instead of the span, threshold ignored).

*Deliberately not claimed: that this fixes it.* The previous claim of
exactly this shape — that a particular presentation would keep review
critical — was falsified on first contact. Whether gap lines actually
induce evaluation is unknown until the next batch is reviewed, and the
honest test is to ask again afterwards rather than to assume.

[[file:~/.claude/plans/session-resume-continuity-guard.md][Plan]]

Captured 2026-08-04, observed live and confirmed with real evidence,
not just a one-off guess: immediately after deliberately clocking out
(via the sibling heading above's manual recovery, with no task
actually being worked on — this conversation was pure "care and
feeding" of the project plan, not implementation work), the very next
prompt silently clocked back in on the unrelated =PLANNING TODO state=
heading (ID b95b9fba-f78e-48fe-8546-988709cce309). Root cause:
=session-resume= (the =UserPromptSubmit= hook) unconditionally calls
=org-clock-in-last=, which resumes whichever heading is most recent in
the *global, shared* =org-clock-history= — with no check on whether
*this session* is the one that put it there.

This is broader than "no task in view this turn," and confirmed to
also bite genuinely concurrent sessions, not just idle/maintenance
ones: a =ps= check during this same conversation found two real
=claude= CLI processes running concurrently (separate terminals), and
the =PLANNING TODO state= heading's own =:SESSIONS:= history showed a
*different* session ID pausing/resuming its clock at one point — not
because that session was doing =PLANNING=-state work (confirmed:
=b95b9fba= appears nowhere in =config.el=, so no implementation code
for that feature has landed from *any* session), but almost certainly
that session's own ordinary turn-boundary hook grabbing the same
shared global clock via the same blind =org-clock-in-last= call.
Because the clock is one global resource, *any* session's resume can
silently inherit and misattribute time to whatever heading happens to
sit at the head of =org-clock-history=, regardless of who set it
=DOING= or whether anyone is actually touching it. The existing
session-id-ownership fix (see "Concurrent Claude Code sessions share
one global org-clock", ID 337f7fb2-b9e9-4c02-82dd-d88e60df364b) only
guards a clock that's *actively running* from being paused/stolen by a
different session mid-flight — it does nothing to stop an *idle*
clock from being resumed onto the wrong heading by whichever session's
=UserPromptSubmit= happens to fire next.

Concrete fix direction (sharper than originally captured): make
=session-resume= conditional on session continuity — only call
=org-clock-in-last= if the clock's most recent close (the last
=:SESSIONS:= =Paused= entry, or the session-id already recorded by the
337f7fb2 work) belongs to *this same session's* ID; otherwise leave it
clocked out and require an explicit =org_clock_in= once real work
actually starts on some heading.

Related, same "single shared global clock" theme, distinct root
causes — worth planning together but not assuming they're one fix:
[[id:53b0047d-c55c-486c-8eed-ba4994d97a1a][Direct file writes to a live org buffer can desync org-clock-marker]]
(external writes corrupting Emacs's in-memory marker) and
[[id:d150c02e-06fe-4514-bf69-e2cc5d8df4c7][org_clock_in doesn't record clock ownership, unlike session-resume]]
(most clock-start paths never record an owner in the first place, so
this bug's own "idle clock" precondition is the common case, not the
exception).

*Cancelled 2026-08-12 by
[[id:e51d6ba1-cc1d-4745-8aa7-e4b1183a230b][e51d6ba1]].* Superseded by
shipped work, not deferred. =bin/hooks/session-resume= no longer calls
=org-clock-in-last=, or reaches Emacs at all: it appends a bare =resume=
guidepost to the session's own queue file and exits. A guidepost names
no heading, so there is no wrong heading left to inherit — attribution
comes from the surrounding =clock_in=/=clock_out= events at review time.
=claude-code-ide-org-session-pause=/=-resume= were deleted at the
2026-08-11 cutover ([[id:feba67eb-35b3-48bd-a892-8ecd47ca52e0][feba67eb]],
commit =220ba78=); the hook script's own header names this heading as
the bug it removed. The failure mode documented here remains the
clearest statement of why that cutover was worth doing.

[[file:~/.claude/plans/clock-in-ownership-recording.md][Plan]]

Captured 2026-08-05, hit live, then re-confirmed and sharpened
2026-08-05 with a direct empirical check. Original finding: manually
clocking a heading in via the =org_clock_in= MCP tool
(=claude-code-ide-org-clock-in=) logs a plain "Resumed" =:SESSIONS:=
entry with no session-id, and never sets
=claude-code-ide-org--clock-owner-session-id=, unlike
=claude-code-ide-org-session-resume=.

*Actual scope, confirmed by exhaustively grepping every call site*:
=(org-clock-in)= is only ever invoked from two places —
=claude-code-ide-org-clock-in= (line ~362) and
=claude-code-ide-org--trigger-auto-clock-in= (line ~1596, fired on
*any* =DOING=/=PLANNING= transition via =org-trigger-hook=, so also
on every =org_set_todo= call and every hand-edit). Meanwhile
=claude-code-ide-org--clock-owner-session-id= is only ever *set* from
one place: =claude-code-ide-org-session-resume=. So owner-recording
covers exactly one of the three ways a clock can start — the
*resume-after-pause* case — while the more common case (transitioning
a heading straight to =DOING=/=PLANNING=) is unowned by construction.
Checked the =337f7fb2= DONE writeup: it only ever describes threading
=session_id= through =session-pause=/=-resume=, never claims trigger-
hook coverage — so this is an honest original scope gap, not a
regression.

*Live-verified, not just theorized*: while another session had a
genuine =PLANNING= heading actively clocked (ID
4cda6bf7-441b-47b2-b3d5-b8c7e7a207a5, set via =org_set_todo=, the
"proper" path), a direct =emacsclient= query showed
=claude-code-ide-org--clock-owner-session-id= =nil= while
=claude-code-ide-org--planning-owner-session-id= correctly held that
session's ID — same heading, same instant, one guard fully engaged,
the other completely absent. =337f7fb2='s own guard is deliberately
permissive when no owner is recorded ("the correct fallback for the
ordinary single-session case, not merely a stopgap," per its own
docstring) — so this isn't broken protection, it's protection that
was never wired to the common code path.

Sharper fix direction than originally captured: the precedent already
exists in this exact codebase.
=claude-code-ide-org--maybe-record-planning-owner= (a =PostToolUse=
hook matched on =org_set_todo=, reading =session_id= straight from its
own hook payload) already solves the identical problem for
=planning-owner-session-id=. The same hook — or a sibling of it — can
set =clock-owner-session-id= too, whenever the requested state is
=DOING=/=PLANNING=, without needing to instrument the trigger hook or
=org_clock_in= itself. =org_clock_in='s own missing session-id is a
narrower, separate case (no =PostToolUse= payload carries a =state=
field for a bare clock-in call) worth a smaller, second fix alongside
it.

Related, same "single shared global clock" theme:
[[id:582cc7f4-41a2-4666-ad3f-1b76b459147e][session-resume blindly inherits any session's last-clocked heading]]
and
[[id:53b0047d-c55c-486c-8eed-ba4994d97a1a][Direct file writes to a live org buffer can desync org-clock-marker]]
— three distinct root causes in the same subsystem, worth planning
together, not assumed to be one fix.

*Cancelled 2026-08-12 by
[[id:e51d6ba1-cc1d-4745-8aa7-e4b1183a230b][e51d6ba1]].* Both halves are
structurally gone rather than fixed. =--clock-owner-session-id= and
=--planning-owner-session-id= were deleted at the 2026-08-11 cutover
([[id:feba67eb-35b3-48bd-a892-8ecd47ca52e0][feba67eb]], commit
=220ba78=) — they survive only inside =config.el='s tombstone comment —
along with =--maybe-record-planning-owner=, the =PostToolUse= hook this
heading proposed reusing. =org_clock_in= now validates an =:ID:= and
opens no clock, so there is no ownership left to record.

The want behind the heading is better served than the fix it proposed:
=bin/hooks/queue-append= stamps =session_id=, =agent_id=, =agent_type=
and =source= on *every* event, and the queue is keyed per session by
filename — so attribution is recorded per event and survives an Emacs
restart, which no global variable did. Caveat worth carrying forward:
as of 2026-08-12 the =agent_id=/=agent_type= fields have never been
populated in 347 events, so that half is designed but unexercised.

[[file:~/.claude/plans/bookkeeping-noise-audit.md][Plan]]

Captured 2026-08-05, raised in conversation: when a session has been
explicitly told to suppress its own clocking for a while (as this one
was), other concurrent sessions' ordinary activity can still write
real =:LOGBOOK:=/=:SESSIONS:= deltas into headings this session
touches or observes — visible throughout this same session (the
=PLANNING TODO state= heading and the notes.org review-task heading
both picked up cross-session clock churn while under the
suppression). The open question: at commit time, should a
clocking-suppressed session specifically double-check that whatever
clock/session bookkeeping deltas are about to be committed are
*genuine* (real, attributable work — its own or another session's)
rather than side-effect noise the suppressed session itself
incidentally observed or triggered, before folding them into a commit
under this session's authorship?

Not yet clear whether this needs new tooling (e.g. a pre-commit diff
review step specific to =:LOGBOOK:=/=:SESSIONS:= hunks) or is purely a
standing-instruction-level judgment call for whoever is about to
commit — same register as other "only the model/user can decide"
rules already in CLAUDE.md. Related to, but broader than, the sibling
heading above (that one is about a specific missing ownership
mechanism; this one is about what to do with the resulting mess at
commit time, regardless of whether that mechanism ever gets fixed).

Also substantial overlap with
[[id:3cb3f955-f10a-47cd-84ab-e629d73ea59d][Org skill: commit a newly-captured TODO immediately, when safe]] —
that heading already raised the same underlying question in the
abstract before this one found a concrete incident. See its own
2026-08-05 update.

*Second concrete incident, 2026-08-06 — a lost interval, not observed
noise, and a root cause none of the recorded incidents cover.* Found by
running exactly the pre-commit audit this heading proposes, during the
Phase 0 verification for
[[id:3d576d29-747f-40b9-a5b3-ecc76679daad][3d576d29]]. Sequence: clocked
in on =3d576d29= at 22:35; a live =emacsclient= probe set =DOING= on a
scratch heading, which fired
=claude-code-ide-org--trigger-auto-clock-in= and moved the clock into
the scratch buffer; recovered with =org-clock-cancel=, then re-clocked
=3d576d29= at ~22:43 and clocked out at 22:45. Both =org_clock_in= and
=org_clock_out= reported success. The heading ends up with:

: CLOCK: [2026-08-06 Thu 22:35]--[2026-08-06 Thu 22:40] =>  0:05

— and *no* second interval for 22:43-22:45. =:SESSIONS:= brackets the
full arc correctly (=Resumed 22:37= / =Paused 22:45=); only the CLOCK
interval vanished. Roughly two minutes, so materially irrelevant; the
point is the failure mode, not the magnitude.

*Root cause found 2026-08-07, correcting the paragraph above:* nothing
to do with =org-clock-cancel=, and not a bug — it is documented,
deliberate behavior. =claude-code-ide-org-clock-out= calls
=claude-code-ide-org-consolidate-history= on every clock-out, which
rounds each closed interval to the nearest 5 minutes
(=claude-code-ide-org--round-time-to-5-minutes=, config.el:900; ties
round *up*) and then drops anything that becomes zero-length
(=--consolidate-logbook-text=, config.el:991, mirroring org's own
=org-clock-out-remove-zero-time-clocks= intent after rounding). 22:43
rounds to 22:45; 22:45 rounds to 22:45; zero; dropped. The earlier
interval survived only because 22:35→22:41 rounded to 22:35→22:40.

Generalized, the rule is: *any interval shorter than about 2.5 minutes
that does not straddle a 5-minute boundary disappears silently on
clock-out.* That is a much broader exposure than one incident — it
applies to every short clock the tools have ever closed. Whether the
5-minute granularity is still the right trade is now a live question
rather than a settled one, and it is decided for the new architecture
in [[id:32272061-1d78-4726-b13b-90338edb2ba5][32272061]]'s plan: apply
writes exactly the endpoints the human confirms, with no rounding and
no zero-drop.

What still makes it worth recording separately: every other incident
catalogued here is about *cross-session* interference or a desynced
marker. This one is single-session, sequential, and purely a
consequence of this project's own consolidation policy — no
concurrency involved at all. Deliberately not "fixed" by
hand-writing the missing line: CLAUDE.md forbids editing CLOCK entries
directly, and fabricating an interval to make the record look tidy is
the exact "confidently wrong" record
[[id:b5f7c5c7-7ad6-4c68-9cce-3479db1f1644][b5f7c5c7]] exists to
prevent.

Note the incident is also mild evidence *for* this heading's premise:
the audit caught it, and it would otherwise have been committed
unnoticed inside a 268-line documentation diff.

*Cancelled 2026-08-12 by
[[id:e51d6ba1-cc1d-4745-8aa7-e4b1183a230b][e51d6ba1]], along the line
[[id:b5f7c5c7-7ad6-4c68-9cce-3479db1f1644][b5f7c5c7]] predicted:* its
mechanism-approach "likely folds into the new review UI rather than
standing alone." All three parts of the premise dissolved. "A
clocking-suppressed session" has no referent — no session clocks at all
since the 2026-08-11 cutover. =:SESSIONS:= no longer exists, and the
only automatic =:LOGBOOK:= writers left fire from =org-todo=, which now
runs only inside the human-driven apply or a human's own hand-edit. And
the genuine-vs-noise judgment is now made *before* anything lands, in
the review buffer with session and timing visible, which is what this
proposed pre-commit audit was reconstructing after the fact.

The second incident recorded above (the vanished 2-minute interval) was
root-caused separately: =consolidate-history='s 5-minute rounding,
retired in =f0fc4a2=. Apply writes exact confirmed endpoints with
=org-clock-out-remove-zero-time-clocks= bound nil.

The surviving commit-hygiene question is not lost —
[[id:3cb3f955-f10a-47cd-84ab-e629d73ea59d][3cb3f955]] holds the
single-session half and
[[id:2aeb65d6-350e-4c75-811e-4a748044fe2c][2aeb65d6]] the cross-session
one, which found the real hazard to be the shared =.git/index=, not
drawer deltas: a different mechanism from the one hypothesised here.

[[file:~/.claude/plans/send-each-mcp-feature-zesty-bunny.md][Plan]]

*This heading is retrospective, and deliberately not backdated.* The
work ran on 2026-07-28/29; the heading was written 2026-08-12 while
resolving [[id:cce72644-7d5e-4def-a165-0a3b815f482b][cce72644]], because
the plan file had no owner and CLAUDE.md's archive rule is that a plan is
kept iff some heading links it. =:CREATED:= is the moment this heading
was created, per the convention, not the moment the work started — the
real dates are in the ten task headings and in the plan file itself.

*What it was.* Orchestration, not design: ten tasks in TODO.org's then
"New MCP tools" section and its MCP-adjacent siblings already carried
fully worked-out checklists, and the plan covered getting all ten built
in isolated worktrees and integrated back one at a time without losing
work or breaking =bin/test=. Written 2026-07-28 21:23; the first task
was archived 2026-07-29 01:57.

*Outcome: all ten shipped, and all ten are archived in DONE.org* —
=org_capture=, =org_clock_report=, =org_refile=,
=org_sort_children=/=org_move_sibling=, the
=org-trigger-hook=/=org-blocker-hook= pair and its config-test.el
extension, the tool-call audit log, surface-current-clock-state, the
PreToolUse transition guard, clock-change notifications, and the
SessionStart context hook. Only five carried an =:ID:= at plan time; the
other five were =(none yet)= in the plan's own table and were created as
the work reached them.

*No clock or =:LOGBOOK:= here, on purpose.* Every one of those ten
headings carries its own intervals, and org's clocktable sums a subtree
by plain addition — so time recorded on an umbrella is *additive* with
the children's rather than a roll-up of it. Same reasoning as
[[id:ab75d6d2-0e59-405d-92c6-2c67488db133][ab75d6d2]]. These ten are not
even children of this heading, so any interval here would be pure
double-count.

*Superseded in one respect, worth knowing before reusing it.* The plan's
load-bearing constraint — clock and state changes are coordinator-only,
one task at a time, because org's clock is a single global resource that
subagents in isolated worktrees cannot safely touch — is exactly the
problem [[id:b5f7c5c7-7ad6-4c68-9cce-3479db1f1644][b5f7c5c7]]'s event
queue replaced. The worktree orchestration still stands; the clocking
discipline around it does not.

Surfaced 2026-08-11 by =bin/sync-plans=, which archives a plan only when
some heading in TODO.org or DONE.org links it — so org membership is the
rule, and a plan nothing links stays outside version control and gets
reported rather than silently swept in. Four are in that state, and all
four are this project's work:

- =parsed-gliding-corbato.md= — *byte-identical to* =review-and-cutover.md=,
  written twenty-one minutes earlier on 2026-08-07. An orphan left behind
  when the auto-generated slug was replaced by a meaningful name. Almost
  certainly just delete it; confirm nothing links it first.
- =cheerful-whistling-sketch.md= — "Fix org-agenda-files resolving to
  nothing (agenda + org_query/org_clock_report)".
- =send-each-mcp-feature-zesty-bunny.md= — "Parallelize the 10 pending
  MCP-tool tasks across worktrees".
- =warp-mcp-proxy-emacs.md= — the Warp proxy investigation, whose outcome
  CLAUDE.md already describes; its heading is archived in DONE.org
  (=6a6d5b4e=) but carries no Plan link.

For the three real ones the fix is a Plan link on the owning heading,
per CLAUDE.md's rule that a plan file's existence and its link are
supposed to arrive together. Their absence is evidence the rule was
added after some of this work, not that it was ignored.

*Worth doing before the next plan revision,* because the archive only
covers what is linked: an unlinked plan is the one case where a revision
still overwrites history with no way back — the exact gap the archive
was built to close.

*Outcome, 2026-08-12.* =bin/sync-plans= now reports *0 unlinked at
source*, 26 in sync. Two linked, two retired:

- =parsed-gliding-corbato.md= — *deleted.* Confirmed byte-identical to
  =review-and-cutover.md=, which is already archived in =plans/=, so no
  content was lost, and confirmed nothing linked it first. Exactly as
  this heading predicted.
- =cheerful-whistling-sketch.md= — *linked* from
  [[id:74f24402-978e-4c66-ac97-996f387c0ddb][74f24402]] in DONE.org, the
  org-agenda-files fix. The one case that went as written.
- =warp-mcp-proxy-emacs.md= — *deleted*, on the user's call.
- =send-each-mcp-feature-zesty-bunny.md= — *linked* from a new
  retrospective heading,
  [[id:3d862c6c-6d03-4fe9-9923-067966ef943a][3d862c6c]], also on the
  user's call.

*This heading was wrong about two of the four, and the errors are the
interesting part.*

1. It said 6a6d5b4e "carries no Plan link." It does — to
   =use-pipx-instead-use-starry-metcalfe.md=, which is archived.
   =warp-mcp-proxy-emacs.md= is a *second, earlier* plan for the same
   heading: the proxy approach abandoned once the real bug turned out to
   be the =200=-vs-=202= response. So the choice was never "add the
   missing link"; it was "what do you do when one heading has two
   plans," which CLAUDE.md's *single* permanent link rule does not
   cover, since it assumes revisions reuse one file. Retired rather than
   double-linked — the heading already links the plan that reflects what
   shipped, and both its own body and CLAUDE.md narrate why the proxy
   was unnecessary.
2. It assumed all three "real ones" had owning headings. The
   parallelization plan had none: its ten tasks are archived flat in
   DONE.org and the "New MCP tools" section that grouped them no longer
   exists, so archiving dissolved the only structure that could have
   owned it. Hence a new heading rather than a link.

*Correction, same day, before this claim spread any further.* The
paragraph here originally read "archiving flattens — a plan scoped to a
section loses its owner the moment that section's members are archived
out." *That is false*, and it was asserted without checking:

- =org-archive-save-context-info= includes =olpath= by default and is
  writing it. 18 of DONE.org's 22 archived headings carry
  =:ARCHIVE_OLPATH:=, and all ten MCP-tool tasks record
  =Roadmap/New MCP tools=. The outline path is preserved, not lost. The
  four without one were archived from level 1, where there was no path.
- What actually removed the section was =b716d37= (2026-08-04),
  "Reflect completed clock-subsystem work back into the roadmap" — a
  deliberate manual restructuring that deleted the =* Roadmap= wrapper
  and promoted every section a level. Archiving behaved correctly
  throughout; a hand edit a week later did the removing.

*What is actually true, and it is narrower:* a plan spanning several
headings has no linkable owner, because =sync-plans= requires a link and
a grouping heading is structural — it carries no =:ID:= by convention
and gets deleted when it empties. So the fix is a convention, not a
mechanism: *create an umbrella heading with an =:ID:= when a plan spans
several tasks*, rather than reconstructing one later from the plan's own
table. That much still belongs in
[[id:02aaae22-0958-4c0f-b5bb-2cbea32416ae][02aaae22]].

*Worth noting how the wrong version nearly survived.* The first check
run against DONE.org reported =org_capture= as having no
=:ARCHIVE_OLPATH:= while a =sed= of the same heading printed the
property two lines above — the script tested list membership of a whole
line where it needed a substring. Same shape as the drawer-scoped grep
failures already recorded above: a wrong answer that looks like a
finding.

*Consolidated 2026-08-11, and the heading retitled to match.* This was
"capture bare headings; apply the keyword at ingestion." Two other
headings turned out to describe edits to the same four lines of the same
function, so they are folded in here:
[[id:cdcc065c-628d-4350-b1ba-fcf686e9c4c1][cdcc065c]] (=org_capture= omits
=:CREATED:=), now =CANCELLED= as a separate task, and the unset
=claude-code-ide-org-capture-file=, whose heading is deleted since
nothing linked to it. The whole of =org_capture= is one template string:

: (format "* TODO %%i\n:PROPERTIES:\n:ID:       %s\n:END:\n" new-id)

Three defects, one edit — treating them as three tasks meant touching
that string three times.

=org_capture= currently writes =* TODO %i= — the keyword is hardcoded in
the template, not a parameter. That asserts a state live while every
other state assertion is queued, which is the cutover's own principle
applied inconsistently.

*Proposed shape (user's, 2026-08-11):* capture writes a bare heading —
=:ID:=, =:CREATED:=, no keyword. Ingestion applies the keyword through
=org-todo= inside the interactive apply, which makes it a genuine
transition and lets org write the creation entry natively.

This is the more conservative split than the "creation *is* a =capture=
event" sketch in
[[id:d9132c57-9dcf-47e9-ba74-7f5a1ced3ae5][d9132c57]]: the heading still
lands immediately, so its =:ID:= is usable and it can be linked and
refiled at once; only the *keyword* defers.

*Verified the mechanism, 2026-08-11*, against the real =#+TODO:= header:
a bare heading taken to =NEXT= or =DOING= produces a native
=- State "NEXT" from [ts]= entry. Taken to =TODO= it produced nothing,
because =TODO= was the one keyword carrying no =!= marker. That was a
hard prerequisite and is now resolved by
[[id:90a5a0cf-a81d-45dc-a453-0bfe61e3ef93][90a5a0cf]]; the remaining
=:BLOCKER:= is the index tool, for placement rather than logging.

It also makes =d9132c57='s duplicate-=:CREATED:=-into-=:LOGBOOK:= vs.
synthesise-at-read-time question moot for anything captured after the
change: org writes the entry, so neither is needed. Backfill is still
owed for the 56 existing headings.

*Accepted cost, confirmed with the user:* between capture and ingestion
the heading matches no =todo:= query and appears in no agenda. Judged
acceptable and "even a good cue to ingest and apply." Agenda visibility
was explicitly ruled out as a concern.

*Second folded defect: no =:CREATED:=.* The template writes only =:ID:=,
against the project's own rule that every heading creation stamps
=:CREATED:=. A bare heading needs it *more*, not less — with no keyword
and no creation entry until ingestion, the property is the only record
that the heading exists and when.

*Third folded defect: capture can only target a file, not a position.*
=(file <file-spec>)= is the least specific target org offers, so
everything lands at top level in whatever file
=claude-code-ide-org-capture-file= names — and that defcustom is =nil=,
so it currently falls through to =org-default-notes-file=,
=~/org/notes.org=, outside the repo entirely. Setting the defcustom alone
would just aim the imprecision at a better file.

*Corrected 2026-08-11, by =org_outline= on its first real call.* This
paragraph previously claimed all three defects were latent because
=~/org/notes.org= contained *zero* captured headings and the tool had
"never been used in anger." Both statements were false, and the error
was methodological: the check was =grep -c '^\* TODO '=, which matches
only the =TODO= keyword, so a captured heading later moved to =DOING=
slipped past it. The structural index showed it immediately — which is
the case [[id:9f3c35c7-0229-4cd6-908b-779267ec9b97][9f3c35c7]] was built
for, arriving about an hour after that heading was written.

*Retracted the same day, one revision later.* The correction above then
over-claimed in the other direction, asserting "the tool has been used
and the damage is real." One heading was observed in =~/org/notes.org=
carrying =:ID:= =780d807e-d441-452f-a407-520225efb3c6= and nothing else
— no =:CREATED:=, top-level, exactly the template's shape — and that
shape was read as proof of provenance. It is not: a hand-made heading, a
heading predating the =:CREATED:= convention, or =org-id-get-create= on
something existing all produce the same thing. The user, asked, described
the file's contents as "pure noise" and cleared it; =notes.org= is now
empty and, being outside the repo, has no git history to re-examine. So
whether =org_capture= has *ever* produced a heading is unresolved and now
unresolvable from evidence.

Worth stating plainly because the paragraph above and this one are the
second and third revisions of the same claim within an hour, all three
correcting in the same direction — asserting more than the evidence
carried. The underlying move each time was filling an unknown with a
plausible value instead of marking it unknown.

*What holds independent of that file's contents:* =notes.org= is in
=org-agenda-files= and =claude-code-ide-org--tracked-files= — still true
now that it is empty — so it is a live capture target that this
project's own tools read, and the earlier claim that it was invisible to
them was wrong on structural grounds, not evidential ones.

*A scope gap that survives the retraction, because it is deductive
rather than evidential.*
[[id:9d2fcdad-9bf7-47b6-8018-223b13ec4577][9d2fcdad]] deleted all 49
=:SESSIONS:= drawers and reports none remaining — true of TODO.org and
DONE.org, 0 each. But that sweep ran over the *repo's* files, and
=notes.org= is tracked without being in the repo, so it was never in
scope. A drawer was in fact observed there before the file was cleared;
even without that observation the gap stands, since the two file sets
differ and nothing reconciles them. Any future sweep over "our org
files" inherits the same blind spot, and =org-agenda-files= is the set
that matters, not the working tree.

Counting them needs an anchored =^:SESSIONS:$=: a bare
=grep -c ':SESSIONS:'= reports *56* in TODO.org by matching prose
mentions of the drawer, which reads as a failed retirement. Exactly the
trap the org skill already warns about — prefer =org-element-map= over
line regexps so a drawer name in prose is never matched as a drawer.

*Placement design, settled with the user 2026-08-11.* An optional target
accepting either an =:ID:= or a refile-style outline path
(=TODO.org/Skill logic=), resolved through the vocabulary
=org-refile-get-targets= already produces — not a new category concept,
and not an ad-hoc exception to "IDs, never titles." The level-1
categories carry no =:ID:= by deliberate convention, so an outline path
is the *only* way to address them; that they are few, stable,
human-curated and never refiled is what makes titles safe here
specifically. Omitting the target keeps today's append-at-top-level
behaviour, which is the honest fallback for "placement unknown" and
removes any need for an inbox heading.

*Implemented 2026-08-11.* The template now writes =* %i= with =:ID:= and
=:CREATED:= and no keyword, and =org_capture= takes an optional
=target=. =:CREATED:= is formatted in elisp rather than via the
template's =%U= escape, for the reason
[[id:cdcc065c-628d-4350-b1ba-fcf686e9c4c1][cdcc065c]] gave: an escape
that fails to expand leaves a literal =%U= behind and still satisfies a
naive is-the-property-present check.

*Deviation from the placement design above, deliberate.* The plan said
the target would accept "a refile-style outline path
(=TODO.org/Skill logic=), resolved through the vocabulary
=org-refile-get-targets= already produces." What shipped accepts an
=:ID:= or the *exact title of a top-level category*. The reason is that
refile-target strings escape =/= inside headings as =\\/= — this file
has a heading containing =NEXT/TODO= that renders as =NEXT\\/TODO= —
so splitting a path on =/= is wrong in a way that would only surface on
particular headings. Matching a level-1 title exactly sidesteps the
parsing entirely and covers both real cases: categories, which have no
=:ID:=, and any ID-bearing parent. Full path support can come later if a
level-2 target is ever wanted; nothing needs it today.

An unknown target *errors* rather than falling back to the end of the
file. A caller that named a destination and silently got a different one
is worse off than one that got an error.

*Still outstanding, and not Claude's to do:*
=claude-code-ide-org-capture-file= is a defcustom set in
=~/.config/doom/config.el=, outside this repo, and it is still =nil= —
so captures continue to land in =org-default-notes-file=. The tool is
correct; the target is not yet pointed at this project. That one line is
the user's to write.

*Verified:* =bin/test= 167/167 — three existing capture tests updated to
the new contract (they asserted =^\* TODO= and a return string ending at
the =:ID:=), six new ones covering the absent keyword, the =:CREATED:=
stamp and its =%U= trap, both target forms, the refusal, and the
omitted-target append. Live against a scratch capture file, all three
paths behaved: =Tooling= demoted the entry to =**= beneath that
category, an omitted target appended at =*=, and a bad target returned
an error with nothing written.

*Scope note: capture is a minority path in this project.* Nine headings
were created on 2026-08-11 and every one was placed correctly by text
editing; =org_capture= was not used once. Its pitch — quick-add without
reading the file — does not survive a house style where headings carry
bodies, cross-links and =:BLOCKER:=s. It still earns its keep for
[[id:7fa68d5c-b6c0-43df-85c6-764b1d56511f][7fa68d5c]]'s no-Emacs
fallback, for a passing mention in a session about something else, and
for immediate =:ID:= registration. Build the smallest thing that makes
it correct, not a parameter surface sized as though it were the primary
way headings get made.

A read-only MCP tool returning one line per heading — level, TODO
keyword, title, =:ID:=, tags, and whether a =:BLOCKER:= is set — as an
index for answering "what already exists here" and "where does this
belong" without reading the file.

*Measured on TODO.org, 2026-08-11:* 280,079 bytes and 82 headings (7 at
level 1, 45 at level 2, 30 at level 3; 70 carry an =:ID:=) reduce to
7,384 bytes of index, or 5,394 with =DONE=/=CANCELLED= filtered out. A
38x reduction, and the prototype that produced it is most of the
implementation.

: Skill logic
:   DONE Enforce a single NEXT action per level of the task tree  {05da96ad}  :code:
:   MAYBE Make org-blocker-hook actually consult :BLOCKER:  {087e73e9}  :code:
:   TODO Fall back to the queue when org_capture cannot reach Emacs  {7fa68d5c}  :code:

*The motivating case is not placement.* It is that three separate times
on 2026-08-11 a session re-derived something this file already knew —
[[id:cdcc065c-628d-4350-b1ba-fcf686e9c4c1][cdcc065c]],
[[id:5e2a1c04-7b3f-4d21-9c88-2f6e0a91b7d3][5e2a1c04]] and
[[id:d9132c57-9dcf-47e9-ba74-7f5a1ced3ae5][d9132c57]]'s content were each
worked out from scratch and presented as new findings. The cause was not
carelessness in any single instance: checking meant reading 280 KB to
answer a one-line question, which is not viable mid-task, so it kept not
happening. A 7 KB index makes "check what is already known" affordable
enough to become routine, which is the only way that discipline actually
holds.

*Design.* Parameters: =scope= (a file, or a subtree =:ID:= to index just
that branch), =max_depth=, and =active_only= to drop finished states.
Implementation is =org-map-entries= over
=claude-code-ide-org--tracked-files=, the same file list =org_query= and
the recovery check already use. No new dependencies.

*Complementary to =org_query=, not overlapping.* =org_query= answers
"which headings match this predicate" and returns a flat list;
=org_outline= answers "what is the shape of this file and what is in it"
and preserves hierarchy. Neither subsumes the other — the flat list
cannot tell you where a heading sits, and the tree cannot filter by
arbitrary predicate.

*Emit full =:ID:=s, not the 8-character prefixes the prototype shows.*
The prototype truncates for readability, but every other tool in this
project takes a full =:ID:= argument, so a truncated index would force a
second lookup on every use and quietly defeat the point. The cost is
about 2 KB more on this file, which is nothing against 280 KB.

*Landmines to clear before implementing:*
- =org-map-entries= with an explicit file list visits those files; make
  sure it does not leave buffers modified or move point in a buffer the
  user has open. This is a read-only tool and must behave like one.
- Output size is unbounded in principle. This file is small, but the
  tool should not be able to return something enormous — =max_depth= and
  =active_only= are the controls, and a documented cap is worth
  considering.
- Heading titles can contain characters that make the output ambiguous
  to skim. The prototype already showed org escaping =!/@= as =!\\/@= in
  refile paths; check what =org-get-heading= returns versus what the
  refile-target machinery returns, and pick one.

*Related: [[id:47c027d2-7b5a-4de0-baf4-f992f3b814bd][47c027d2]] is
blocked on this*, because correct placement at capture time is only
cheap once the index exists.

*Also worth knowing, from the same investigation:*
=org-refile-get-targets= already returns 168 addressable destinations for
this file as =FILE/Outline/Path= strings, *including the level-1
categories* — which carry no =:ID:= by convention and so cannot be
addressed any other way. =org-refile-targets= is already
=((nil :maxlevel . 3) (org-agenda-files :maxlevel . 3))=, and level 3 is
this file's full depth. That is an existing placement vocabulary, used by
=org_refile= today, and it is what =47c027d2='s target parameter should
accept rather than inventing a category concept.

*Implemented 2026-08-11.* =claude-code-ide-org-outline=, registered as
=org_outline=, with =scope= (an =:ID:= for one subtree, a file name for
one file, or omitted for every tracked file), =max_depth=, and
=active_only=. All three arrive as strings and are parsed leniently:
unusable input falls back to the permissive default rather than erroring,
since an over-large index is recoverable and a failed call is not.

*Shipped sizes, which differ from the estimate above.* Full =:ID:=s cost
about 2 KB more than the truncated prototype: 9,451 bytes for the whole
file, 6,900 with =active_only=. Still a 30x reduction against 280 KB, and
worth it — a truncated index would force a second lookup on every use.

*All three landmines cleared before writing code.* =org-map-entries= over
an explicit file list neither moves point nor marks the buffer modified
(measured against a live open TODO.org: point 124975 before and after).
Output size is bounded by the two parameters. And =org-get-heading t t t
t= returns titles unescaped, unlike =org-refile-get-targets=, which
renders =!/@= as =!\\/@= — fine for a completion table, wrong for
something meant to be read.

*A fourth landmine surfaced only in live use, and is the useful part of
this entry.* The first live call came back as a =#("..." 0 11 (...))=
literal: every accessor here reads from the buffer and carries its text
properties, and =concat= propagates them, so the index would have reached
the MCP layer propertized. Three things went wrong in sequence and each
is worth keeping:

1. *The unit tests could not see it.* Under =emacs --batch -Q= no
   font-lock runs, so a scratch org file yields clean strings and the
   assertion passed whether or not the code stripped anything. An inert
   test that looks like a passing one — the third instance in one day of
   a fixture differing from production in exactly the dimension under
   test, after
   [[id:720b2dcf-6af1-45f3-96a7-aa841e5651e1][720b2dcf]]'s =#+TODO:=
   markers and
   [[id:5e2a1c04-7b3f-4d21-9c88-2f6e0a91b7d3][5e2a1c04]]'s content-block
   payloads. The fix was to propertize the fixture by hand.
2. *The obvious fix was wrong.* Stripping =org-get-heading= alone left
   the result propertized anyway, because =org-get-todo-state=,
   =org-get-tags= and =org-entry-get= all do it too. Caught only because
   the corrected test then failed against the supposedly-fixed code.
3. *The strip belongs at assembly*, over the whole line, not per
   component — one call that cannot be defeated by adding a fourth
   accessor later.

*Verified:* =bin/test= 157/157 (145 pre-existing plus 12 new), the
plain-string test confirmed to fail with the strip removed and pass with
it, and a live call against the real TODO.org returning a plain string.

*Follow-up fix the same evening, found by using the tool.* The first
=[blocked]= marker keyed on the *presence* of a =:BLOCKER:= property.
org-depend treats that property as a durable declaration of dependency,
not a flag it clears when the blocker finishes — so every heading that
ever had one read as blocked permanently. Measured on TODO.org at the
moment it was noticed: *all 10 markers were false*, because all four
referenced headings were =DONE=. Recorded here rather than as a new
heading, since it was found and fixed within the hour and belongs to
this tool's story.

Now resolved rather than asserted: the =:BLOCKER:= value is scanned for
ids, each is looked up, and the marker distinguishes three cases —
=[blocked]= when a named blocker is unfinished, =[blocked?]= when a
dependency exists but cannot be resolved (a dangling id, or a form like
=previous-sibling= that names none), and nothing when all are finished.
Unresolvable is deliberately not collapsed into satisfied; collapsing
the two is how the first version went wrong in the other direction.

Two incidental findings from the survey. TODO.org carries *one*
=:BLOCKER:= written as a bare id with no =ids(...)= wrapper, which
org-depend itself would not honour — the reader handles it anyway,
because reporting that heading as dependency-free would be worse than
reading a malformed value generously. And finishedness is tested against
this file's own =--outline-finished-keywords= rather than
=org-done-keywords=, which is buffer-local and would be nil in the wrong
buffer, quietly reporting every blocker as still open.

*Verified:* =bin/test= 161/161. Three of the five new tests confirmed to
fail against the presence-only marker; the other two pass either way,
because the old code marked *everything* blocked and so matched the
positive cases by accident — kept as pins, not counted as evidence.
Live, the real TODO.org went from 10 =[blocked]= markers to 0.

- State "CANCELLED"  from "TODO"       [2026-08-11 Tue 18:19] \\
  folded into 47c027d2 as one template edit
:END:

CLAUDE.md is unambiguous: "any newly created org heading gets a
=:CREATED:= property in its property drawer, stamped with an inactive
timestamp at creation time, alongside its =:ID:=. Applies to every
heading creation." The one tool whose entire job is creating headings
does not do it.

Its template, built fresh per call in =claude-code-ide-org-capture=, is
exactly:

: "* TODO %i\n:PROPERTIES:\n:ID:       %s\n:END:\n"

Title, =:ID:=, nothing else. Confirmed 2026-08-11 by grep: the string
=CREATED= appears nowhere in config.el, so nothing adds it afterwards
either. Every =:CREATED:= currently in TODO.org is there because a human
or Claude hand-wrote it while composing the heading in Elisp — which is
also why the gap has gone unnoticed: the path that honours the rule is
the path that bypasses the tool.

*Fix:* add =:CREATED:  %%U= to the template. org-capture's =%U= expands
to an inactive timestamp with date and time, which is precisely the
convention's format. Note the doubled =%%=: the template is assembled
with =format=, which is why the existing title escape is written =%%i=.
Match the drawer's existing alignment (=:CREATED:= followed by two
spaces) so captured headings are indistinguishable from hand-written
ones.

*Test:* the existing capture coverage should additionally assert a
=:CREATED:= that parses as an inactive timestamp — not merely that the
string is present, since a template escape that silently fails to expand
would leave a literal =%U= and still match a naive check.

Worth reading with [[id:7fa68d5c-b6c0-43df-85c6-764b1d56511f][7fa68d5c]], which
records the larger reason this matters less than it looks: almost
nothing in this project is captured through this tool.

*Folded into
[[id:47c027d2-7b5a-4de0-baf4-f992f3b814bd][47c027d2]], 2026-08-11.*
=CANCELLED= as a *separate* task, not abandoned: the missing =:CREATED:=
is real and still gets fixed, but it turned out to be one of three
defects in the same four-line template string, alongside the hardcoded
=TODO= keyword and the file-only capture target. Treating them
separately meant editing that string three times. This heading stays in
place rather than being deleted because five other headings link to it;
the analysis above is still the reference for *why* =:CREATED:= is owed
and how to verify it, and =47c027d2= carries the work.

:PROPERTIES:
:CATEGORY: Tools
:ID:       0308e7d7-06ea-48fb-8579-6a5a43277674
:CREATED:  [2026-08-11 Tue 16:22]
:ARCHIVE_TIME: 2026-08-17 Mon 17:13
:ARCHIVE_FILE: ~/git/claude-code-ide-org/TODO.org
:ARCHIVE_OLPATH: Skill logic
:ARCHIVE_CATEGORY: TODO
:ARCHIVE_TODO: DONE
:END:
:LOGBOOK:
CLOCK: [2026-08-11 Tue 18:16]--[2026-08-11 Tue 18:28] =>  0:12
CLOCK: [2026-08-11 Tue 17:34]--[2026-08-11 Tue 17:36] =>  0:02
- State "DONE"       from "DOING"      [2026-08-11 Tue 16:47] \\
  precondition documented and snippet verified
- State "DOING"      from "TODO"       [2026-08-11 Tue 16:45] \\
  add modified-buffer precondition to org skill
- [2026-08-11 Tue 17:34]--[2026-08-11 Tue 17:36]
- [2026-08-11 Tue 18:16]--[2026-08-11 Tue 18:28]
:END:

Heading creation, tagging and prose edits are text operations by design
— Claude writes the =.org= file on disk directly, and only clock/state
changes go through Emacs. That division is deliberate and still right.
What it lacks is a precondition: nothing checks whether Emacs is holding
a *modified* buffer for the file about to be edited.

*Instance three, 2026-08-11, and the first one Claude caused.* Six new
headings and three body edits were written to TODO.org on disk while
Emacs held a buffer that had been modified — and therefore stale — for
hours. =global-auto-revert-mode= is on but deliberately refuses to
revert a modified buffer, so it had silently stopped tracking the file.
Discovered only because an unrelated =org-id-find= on a
just-written =:ID:= came back nil. Had that not happened, the divergence
would have persisted until something saved or reverted.

Only four characters of the buffer were genuinely unsaved — =maye=,
stray keystrokes appended to a =CLOCK:= duration, exactly the accident
=buffer-read-only= is normally set to prevent. So the resolution was
cheap. It was cheap by luck: any real unsaved work in that buffer would
have forced a genuine three-way merge between disk, buffer, and intent.

*What already guards this, and why it is not enough.* =config.el='s
audit hashing reads straight off disk precisely to catch buffer/disk
divergence ("bit this project twice already", =config.el= ~line 90), but
it detects *after* a mutation rather than preventing one.
=basic-save-buffer= does check =verify-visited-file-modtime= and prompt
=yes-or-no-p= before overwriting a changed file (verified), so
=--review-apply-item='s per-item =save-buffer= cannot silently clobber —
but a prompt is the one thing that must never appear in a
non-interactive path, and it is only reachable at all because apply has
a human present.

*Proposed shape:* the file-level analogue of the reload-precondition
rule in the user's global CLAUDE.md — before text-editing a tracked
=.org= file, establish that Emacs is not holding unsaved changes to it,
and stop and say so if it is. Cheap to check
(=(buffer-modified-p (get-file-buffer f))=), and the answer is the
finding when it comes back non-nil. Belongs in the org skill next to the
existing read-only guidance, which covers the adjacent case (buffer
read-only) but not this one.

*Worth deciding alongside:* whether =global-auto-revert-mode='s refusal
to revert modified buffers should be surfaced somewhere. It is correct
behaviour that produces a silent failure mode — a file the user believes
is auto-reverting quietly stops the moment a stray keystroke marks the
buffer modified.

*Done 2026-08-11.* Added "Before editing: check for an unsaved buffer" to
the org skill, placed ahead of "Editing & transforming" because it is a
precondition to all editing rather than a technique. It gives the
three-field =get-file-buffer=/=buffer-modified-p=/
=verify-visited-file-modtime= check, states that =:modified= non-nil means
*stop and tell the user* — never revert (discards their work) and never
save (discards yours) — and records the incident above as the motivating
case. The auto-revert question folded in there rather than going
elsewhere: the section explains why a modified buffer silently stops
tracking, which is the whole reason the check is needed.

*Verified by running the documented snippet*, not by reading it: against
an open unmodified buffer =(:open t :modified nil :in-sync t)=, and
against a path with no buffer =(:open nil ...)= with no error. That second
case exposed a genuine documentation bug — with no buffer the check
returns =:in-sync nil=, which reads as "out of sync" when it means "not
applicable" — so the text now says to read =:open= first and treat the
other fields as meaningless when it is nil. A snippet that alarms on the
common case would have been worse than no check at all.

*Not tested, and not worth forcing:* whether the skill's own description
causes this section to be consulted at the right moment. That is
trigger-matching, which this project's engineering practices explicitly
exempt from deterministic testing. What is verified is that the content
is correct when read.

[[file:~/.claude/plans/warm-marinating-puddle.md][Plan]]

Captured 2026-08-05 from conversation: how to kick off planning for
every open NEXT/TODO heading in parallel, while getting the resulting
=:SESSIONS:= bookkeeping right, given the constraint (confirmed live,
repeatedly, this same day) that org's clock is a single global
resource shared across every session touching this file.

*Core rule, structural not just cautious*: background planning agents
never transition any heading's TODO keyword and never call
=org_clock_in=/=org_set_todo=-to-=PLANNING=. Both
=claude-code-ide-org--planning-owner-session-id= and
=claude-code-ide-org--clock-owner-session-id= are single global
variables, and =claude-code-ide-org--promote-planning-to-doing=
promotes "whichever heading currently owns the running clock" — so N
simultaneous =PLANNING= owners is structurally impossible, not merely
awkward. There is exactly one clock. Background agents do read-only
research and write only their own plan file
(=~/.claude/plans/<slug>.md=); nothing about that touches the shared
clock, so it is the only part of this safe to genuinely parallelize.

*Write-back* (applying results to =TODO.org= — the Plan link plus a
session-bracketing =:SESSIONS:= note per heading):
- Serialize it: one heading at a time, only after each agent reports
  done.
- Route every write through =emacsclient=/elisp, not a raw external
  file write, even for headings with no clock currently running on
  them — unconditional consistency, not a per-call "is it safe right
  now" check. Directly motivated by
  [[id:53b0047d-c55c-486c-8eed-ba4994d97a1a][Direct file writes to a live org buffer can desync org-clock-marker]].
- Use =claude-code-ide-org--log-session-event= for the synthetic
  =:SESSIONS:= entries rather than hand-writing text — keeps the
  format forward-compatible with
  [[id:2b0988ed-eb92-4fa7-904a-cb2d10941bfd][Reorder :SESSIONS: entries to match :LOGBOOK: ordering]]'s pending
  flip, and guarantees correct drawer-append semantics.
- Re-resolve each heading fresh by =:ID:= at write time
  (=claude-code-ide-org--at-id=, the pattern every existing tool
  already uses) rather than trusting any position cached from when
  the agent was launched — other sessions touch this file constantly,
  demonstrated repeatedly today, including while this very design was
  being written up.
- Tag the synthetic =:SESSIONS:= entry with a distinct synthetic
  identifier, never this orchestrating session's own real
  =session_id= — misattributing unattended background research time
  as this session's own interactive work would be exactly the kind of
  noise
  [[id:782cda6c-111c-454e-93eb-b2b27012078b][Audit for clock/session bookkeeping noise before committing during a clocking-suppressed session]]
  is worried about.
- No =:LOGBOOK:=/CLOCK entries at all, by design — the single-clock
  model cannot represent true parallelism honestly, so don't try.
- Don't auto-commit the resulting batch. Leave it for explicit
  review — finalizing an auto-commit policy here would mean guessing
  at exactly the still-open question in
  [[id:3cb3f955-f10a-47cd-84ab-e629d73ea59d][Org skill: commit a newly-captured TODO immediately, when safe]]
  and [[id:782cda6c-111c-454e-93eb-b2b27012078b][the sibling heading above]].

Motivated concretely, not hypothetically: while this design was being
reviewed in the same conversation, this session's own ordinary
=UserPromptSubmit= resume hook reopened an unrelated heading's clock
*twice* and briefly produced a malformed, timestamp-less =CLOCK:=
line — see
[[id:53b0047d-c55c-486c-8eed-ba4994d97a1a][Direct file writes to a live org buffer can desync org-clock-marker]]'s
"Second, distinct incident" note. That happened from ordinary
incidental multi-session activity, not deliberate parallel load —
strong first-party evidence for why deliberately launching several
background agents at once needs the constraints above, not weaker
ones.

Open questions left for actual planning: exact format/label for the
synthetic =:SESSIONS:= identifier; how many agents to launch per
batch and whether that needs a cap; whether "no clock entries at all"
should extend to *every* unattended/background invocation of this
skill or just this specific batch-planning use case.

*Resolved during planning (2026-08-05):* synthetic identifier is
=<orchestrating-session-id>-bg<N>= (derived from, never equal to, the
real session id); batch size capped at 3; "no clock entries" scoped
to this specific background-planning write-back path only, not
generalized to every background invocation.

*Implementation notes:* added
=claude-code-ide-org-log-background-plan= (id, plan-file, session-id)
plus its =claude-code-ide-org--insert-plan-link= helper, exposed as
the new MCP tool =org_log_background_plan=. Reuses
=claude-code-ide-org--at-id= and =claude-code-ide-org--log-session-event=
exactly as specified above; inserts the Plan link idempotently
(=org-end-of-meta-data t= to land after the property drawer and any
=:SESSIONS:=/=:LOGBOOK:= drawers) and never calls =org-todo=,
=org-clock-in=, or =org-clock-out=. Documented the orchestration
workflow (query → batch of ≤3 background agents → serialized
write-back) as a new section in the org skill
(=.claude/skills/org/SKILL.md=), and added the new tool to CLAUDE.md's
MCP tools table.

*Verified, not just implemented:* four new ERT tests
(=config-test.el=) cover link+:SESSIONS: insertion, idempotency
across repeated calls with different plan-file paths, that TODO
state/clock/owner-vars are untouched, and fresh :ID: re-resolution
under buffer mutation between calls — =bin/test= passes 122/122
(118 pre-existing + 4 new). Also live-reloaded =config.el= into the
running Doom Emacs and ran a manual smoke test against a scratch
heading via =emacsclient=: confirmed the Plan link and a
"Background-planned" =:SESSIONS:= entry appear, no =:LOGBOOK:= entry
or TODO-state change occurs, and a second call with a different
plan-file path does not duplicate the Plan link.
